articles.summary: Olivia Colman stars alongside Alexander Skarsgård in the upcoming film Wicker which has prompted many memes.
articles.body:
New fantasy rom-com Wicker, starring Olivia Colman and Alexander Skarsgård, has sparked a flood of viral memes and tongue-in-cheek jokes on social media ahead of its cinema release.

The film tells the tale of a lonely, ostracised fisherwoman living in a medieval village who hires a basketmaker to mould her a new partner made entirely out of wicker.

Speaking to the BBC at the film's BFI London Film Festival premiere, lead star Olivia Colman admitted she was taken aback by the online frenzy surrounding the film.

"No, literally this has never happened for anything I've done before," she said. "But you put Alexander Skarsgård in an interesting outfit, and everyone is looking."

articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo calls women-focused festival ‘one hundred percent’ political
articles.summary: Olivia Rodrigo confirmed Daisy Chain Fields was "one hundred percent" political, raising $20 million for Planned Parenthood and other charities.
articles.body: Grammy-winning singer Olivia Rodrigo said her women-focused music festival Daisy Chain Fields was "one hundred percent" political, saying critics who disagree with her message "don’t have to buy a ticket." Headlined by Rodrigo, the one-day music festival in Irvine, Calif., featured an all-female lineup, including performances by Chappell Roan, Sarah McLachlan and Stevie Nicks. Net proceeds from Daisy Chain Fields were directed toward nonprofit organizations "dedicated to advancing and advocating for women and girls," including Planned Parenthood, the Center for Reproductive Rights, Baby2Baby and the Black Mamas Matter Alliance. The festival raised $20 million for the women-focused charities and Rodrigo made it clear that she planned the festival with politics in mind. PLANNED PARENTHOOD ACROSS MIDWEST AT RISK DUE TO LACK OF FEDERAL FUNDS AFTER 3 FACILITIES CLOSE IN MICHIGAN "One hundred percent, yes," she told The Hollywood Reporter when asked whether Daisy Chain Fields was political. "But I think it’s also about joy," she added. "I think the two things can exist at the same time, they kind of have to… I think young people have lost hope in our leaders and lost hope in each other. I really wanted to galvanize people and be evidence of what can happen when you come together and are part of something and contribute." The "Drivers License" singer also stated that those who don't agree with the festival's political message don't have to buy a ticket. "Everyone is welcome to come to Daisy Chain. But if you don’t agree with the message that we’re sending, then you don’t have to buy a ticket," she said. ED SHEERAN CONCERTGOERS WARN ARTISTS ABOUT SHARING POLITICAL VIEWS: 'YOU'RE GOING TO ALIENATE' FANS Daisy Chain Fields was inspired by Lilith Fair, an all-female traveling music festival launched in the late 1990s by McLachlan, who was frustrated over the lack of female representation in the music industry. Rodrigo, 23, argued that women had more rights in the 1990s than they do in 2026. "When Lilith Fair was happening 30 years ago, women in America had more rights, had more autonomy over their bodies," the singer said. "I’ve always felt really protective of my young fans, and when I play a show and I look out into the audience and see young girls with their friends or their moms or their families, I feel such a kinship with them," she continued. "And if I could be a small part in making the world a safer and better place for them to grow up and live, that’s what I want." SUPREME COURT TEMPORARILY BLOCKS APPEALS COURT RULING ON ABORTION PILL, RESTORES WIDER ACCESS TO DRUG Rodrigo released her song "Serena Joy" just before the festival. The single is named after a character from "Handmaid’s Tale" who promoted an oppressive regime that eventually deprived her of her own power. The lyrics, including "a tower we built, painted gold on the walls" and "now go bother your neighbors while we do what we wish," have prompted speculation that the song takes aim at President Donald Trump, though Rodrigo declined to confirm that interpretation. "It’s basically a song about complacency," the singer said. "It’s about how an attack on one person’s human rights is an attack on all of our human rights. It’s something I’ve been thinking about a lot." Rodrigo's decision to incorporate politics into her performances drew praise and criticism from political commentators, some of whom argued that her approach alienates fans who do not share her views. Podcast host Ben Ferguson told Fox News Digital that the festival represented the "breathtaking hypocrisy of Hollywood," arguing that Rodrigo was treating her audience like "political minions." SPRINGSTEEN, OTHER STARS SHARE STAGE WITH HARDCORE LEFTIST GROUPS AT MUSIC FEST "These celebrities love preaching tolerance, diversity and inclusion right up until someone dares to disagree with their politics. Then suddenly it’s, ‘Don’t buy a ticket.’ Apparently, everyone is welcome as long as they think exactly like Olivia Rodrigo," Ferguson said. "That’s not inclusion. That’s political arrogance wrapped in a concert tour." But Rodrigo’s willingness to openly embrace politics has also won praise from Democrats, including strategist Kaivan Shroff, who said celebrities who don’t speak out on current events can be viewed as "inauthentic." "This is not some niche artist trying to cultivate a fanbase by leaning into cheap politics. She is making politics part of the art, part of the live show and part of the brand, and at least she is being honest about that and owning it," Shroff told Fox News Digital. "I actually think ‘if you don’t agree, don’t buy a ticket’ is cleaner than pretending the politics are incidental. But there is a tradeoff," he continued. "The minute you tell people the show itself carries a political message, disagreement with that message becomes part of the consumer experience too. You cannot make politics central to the product and then act surprised when the product gets judged politically." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Rodrigo has previously sparred with the Trump administration, condemning the Department of Homeland Security in 2025 after it used her song "All-American B----" in a social media post encouraging illegal immigrants to self-deport from the country. She has also criticized Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) for being "barbaric and cruel." Film critic and Hollywood in Toto founder Christian Toto echoed Ferguson’s concerns, telling Fox News Digital: "In these contentious times, getting hyper political and alienating large swathes of your audience is less than ideal." When reached for comment by Fox News Digital, the White House pointed to an X posting about what it calls "Trump Derangement Syndrome."

articles.title: Festival Nordestino do CTN tem shows, gastronomia e atrações culturais com entrada gratuita em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento acontece até 25 de outubro, na Zona Norte da capital, e celebra tradições dos nove estados do Nordeste. Tierry, Zeza dos Teclados, Thiago Viana e Banda Encantus estão entre as atrações musicais.
articles.summary: Evento acontece até 25 de outubro, na Zona Norte da capital, e celebra tradições dos nove estados do Nordeste. Tierry, Zeza dos Teclados, Thiago Viana e Banda Encantus estão entre as atrações musicais.
articles.body:
Festival Nordestino do CTN tem show de Tierry e comidas típicas — Foto: Divulgação

O Festival Nordestino do Centro de Tradições Nordestinas (CTN) chega à terceira edição com shows, experiências gastronômicas e atividades culturais em São Paulo . O evento acontece de 8 a 25 de outubro, no Bairro do Limão, na Zona Norte da capital, com entrada gratuita.

A programação celebra a música, os sabores e as manifestações culturais dos nove estados nordestinos: Bahia, Maranhão, Piauí, Pernambuco, Rio Grande do Norte, Paraíba, Ceará, Alagoas e Sergipe. As atividades começaram no Dia do Nordestino, comemorado em 8 de outubro, e seguem aos sábados e domingos.

A cada fim de semana, diferentes estados serão homenageados em uma programação temática que inclui apresentações musicais, oficinas, cortejos, danças e manifestações tradicionais da região.

Entre os destaques musicais estão Tierry e Zeza dos Teclados, que se apresentam em 10 de outubro. No dia 17, será a vez de Thiago Viana e Caio Costta. Já em 24 de outubro, o público poderá acompanhar os shows de Raquel dos Teclados e Banda Encantus.

Gastronomia tem pratos típicos e degustações gratuitas

A culinária nordestina também é um dos destaques do festival. Durante a programação gastronômica, os visitantes poderão conhecer a história das receitas, seus ingredientes e modos de preparo. Após as apresentações, pequenas porções dos pratos serão distribuídas gratuitamente ao público.

Entre as receitas previstas estão acarajé, cartola e rubacão. Os restaurantes do CTN também oferecerão opções especiais inspiradas nas culinárias dos nove estados nordestinos, como Maria Isabel, sarapatel, buchada de bode, arrumadinho, carne de sol com macaxeira e baião de dois.

Festival terá atividades sobre a cultura nordestina

Além dos shows e das experiências gastronômicas, o evento contará com atrações voltadas à história, à cultura e ao turismo da região.

A programação inclui o Museu Turístico a Céu Aberto, o Cantinho Nordestino, o Mapa Raízes Nordestinas e o Jogo da Memória Nordestina. As atividades foram planejadas para aproximar o público das referências culturais e históricas dos nove estados.

📅 Quando? De 8 a 25 de outubro; sábados, das 11h às 4h; domingos, das 11h às 23h

📍 Onde? Centro de Tradições Nordestinas (CTN), Rua Jacofer, 615, Bairro do Limão (Zona Norte)

articles.summary: Evento com entrada gratuita será realizado nesta sexta-feira (9) e no sábado (10), a partir das 19h, na Orla de Pirapora.
articles.body:
Quinze pratos fazem parte do festival — Foto: Divulgação

O município de Pirapora , no Norte de Minas, recebe neste fim de semana a terceira edição do Festival de Gastronomia e Arte, realizado pela Prefeitura em parceria com o Sebrae Minas.

Além de experimentar os pratos dos 15 estabelecimentos participantes do Prepara Gastronomia, o público poderá conferir a exposição e a comercialização de artesanatos, ações da Biblioteca Tamboril Itinerante e o III Encontro de Autos Antigos de Pirapora. A programação também inclui apresentações musicais de bandas locais nos dois dias do evento.

Com entrada gratuita, o festival será realizado na Orla de Pirapora, a partir das 19h desta sexta-feira (9) e no sábado (10).

Segundo a analista do Sebrae Minas Kátia Izabel Silva Leite, o trabalho desenvolvido com os empreendimentos do setor de alimentação contribui para valorizar a cultura alimentar e aprimorar a gestão dos negócios.

“O Festival de Gastronomia e Arte de Pirapora se consolidou e já entrou para o calendário oficial de eventos. Estes empreendimentos podem testar novas receitas e utilizar o festival como uma excelente estratégia de posicionamento de suas respectivas marcas e para o acesso a novos clientes”, destaca.

articles.title: Hayden Panettiere's daughter, 11, appears in court amid estate battle
articles.summary: Hayden Panettiere's daughter made a rare court appearance alongside her father, Wladimir Klitschko, amid a legal dispute over the actress's estate.
articles.body:
Hayden Panettiere 's daughter, Kaya , made a rare court appearance amid the legal dispute over her mother's estate.

The 11-year-old attended the Los Angeles Superior Court hearing virtually on Oct. 8 alongside her father, Wladimir Klitschko , Panettiere's former fiancé, according to The Associated Press and People . Kaya reportedly briefly appeared on camera to confirm her identity to the judge.

She was "soft-spoken and composed," People reported. The proceedings centered on Klitschko's request for "immediate" guardianship of Panettiere's estate on behalf of Kaya, the sole beneficiary, alleging "non-family members" have been misappropriating the "Nashville" star's property.

The judge ultimately granted Klitschko temporary guardianship of the estate and set another court date for Dec. 7, noting Kaya would not need to be present.

Hayden Panettiere and Wladimir Klitschko's lasting connection – See photos

Hayden Panettiere, 36, died after suffering cardiac arrest in Greenville, South Carolina . Her ex-fiancé, boxer Wladimir Klitschko, is speaking out about their family's profound shock and grief following the announcement of her death. Klitschko, who holds full custody of their daughter, Kaya, wrote that while Panettiere was "no longer" his partner, she played "an important part" in his life. Look back at their relationship in photos. Here Pannettier stands with Klitschko as he waves to fans after losing the fight against Tyson Fury on Nov. 28, 2015 in Esprit Arena, Dusseldorf, Germany. Klitschko's 11-year reign as heavyweight champion ended that night.

Wladimir Klitschko alleges Hayden Panettiere's estate is at risk

Panettiere met Klitschko in 2009. The couple were engaged in 2013 and welcomed Kaya the following year before splitting in 2018. The former boxing champion later obtained full custody.

Panettiere died Aug. 16 at age 36. The Greenville County Coroner's Office ruled that her death resulted from the "toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine."

Klitschko filed his petition for temporary guardianship of the estate on Sept. 24, stating he "is informed and believes that non-family members previously connected to Hayden have accessed and destroyed Hayden's emails" and "certain items of personal property belonging to Hayden, including jewelry, have disappeared or remain unaccounted for," according to documents previously obtained by USA TODAY.

The filing said his appointment was "urgent and essential" so he could have "the necessary standing to file Hayden's probate petition, and the power to nominate a proposed administrator of Hayden's Estate." Without Klitschko in that position, the petition alleged, there is a "high probability that property belonging to Hayden's estate may be lost, damaged or dissipated before a duly appointed personal representative can be in place to protect it."

Amid the investigation into Panettiere's death, federal agents have accessed her Los Angeles home "and removed property," according to Klitschko. But there is currently no one "authorized to safeguard the interests of Hayden's estate in connection with the investigation, including the return of estate property once it is no longer needed by investigators, and to interface with investigators on behalf of Haden's estate."

The filing further alleged that Panettiere hired a security service to protect her home due to "a documented concern that an individual had gained unauthorized access to Hayden's property." After she died, the home's locks were allegedly changed and her "designer clothing and accessories worn to public appearances have been relocated as a precaution."

Still, the petition added that "it is expected that the individual will continue to try and misappropriate property belonging to Hayden's Estate."

During the Oct. 8 hearing, Klitschko's lawyers reportedly said he will use his power as temporary guardian to "request" and "authorize" law enforcement to investigate and aid in the recovery of the misappropriated property.

articles.title: Dakota Johnson habla sobre su destape integral más vergonzoso: "Lo dejé crecer"
articles.standfirst: En plena promoción de 'Verity' desempolva su pasado con '50 sombras de Grey'
articles.summary: En plena promoción de 'Verity' desempolva su pasado con '50 sombras de Grey'
articles.body: Dakota Johnson está en plena promoción de su nueva película, Verity, y la actriz ha vuelto a dejar una anécdota relacionada con otras interpretaciones que causaron un shock en el ámbito cinematográfico. La actriz que reparte su papel junto a Anne Hathaway y Josh Hartnett, participó en un divertido reto para el canal de YouTube First We Feast. Allí tuvo que elegir entre responder a una pregunta comprometida o enfrentarse a preguntas picantes... La intérprete no se lo pensó dos veces. Aceptó. La cuestión era sencilla: revelar lo más vergonzoso que había hecho para preparar un personaje. Su respuesta desató las risas inmediatas de sus compañeros. En un primer momento, la actriz bromeó asegurando que había sido para Madame Web, aunque enseguida aclaró que en realidad se trataba de la primera entrega de 50 sombras de Grey. "Fue para la primera película. Había una escena de desnudo integral y se suponía que mi personaje nunca se había depilado", desveló Johnson entre risas. La confesión provocó la curiosidad de Anne Hathaway, que le preguntó si no había considerado utilizar una prótesis capilar utilizada habitualmente en cine para este tipo de escenas. La respuesta de Johnson fue tan breve como contundente: "No". Pese a haber participado después en films tan destacados como Suspiria, La hija oscura o Materialistas, Dakota Johnson sigue acumulando titulares vinculados a la saga que la convirtió en una estrella mundial. Y esta última confesión demuestra que el rodaje de 50 sombras de Grey todavía guarda historias capaces de sorprender al público. Johnson también estuvo en el popular programa Saturday Night Live y en él confesó que la película "es un thriller erótico psico-sexual y, ¿sabéis qué? Salir con músicos también lo es", para añadir: “Algunos no llevan zapatos, algunos son terribles en la cama, pero todos están en mi buzón de mensajes privados. Aunque es culpa mía. Algunas personas salen de los conciertos con merchandising y yo salgo de los conciertos con una relación de dos años y medio”, en alusión a cómo comenzó su relación en concreto con Chris Martin.

articles.title: In new Elon Musk documentary, his lieutenants are the most damning voices
articles.summary: ‘Musk,’ the new film from Alex Gibney, features interviews with more than the usual critics of the Tesla and SpaceX CEO.
articles.body:
SAN RAFAEL, Calif. — It's easy to find people with bad things to say about tech magnate Elon Musk, and plenty of those people show up in "Musk," a new documentary about his rise to political and corporate power. What's more surprising in the film are the unflattering statements by some of his own employees, including ones who still work for him.

Some of the harshest scenes in the film, which opens Friday in Los Angeles and New York, are ones in which Musk's lieutenants were recorded on video or in audio as they wielded power on his behalf or discussed what they had already done for him.

Warning: This article includes spoilers for the documentary "Musk."

There are clips of Ashok Elluswamy, a high-ranking Tesla engineer, acknowledging in a videotaped deposition that an infamous hype video he helped put together in 2016 about the company's self-driving capabilities was not an accurate representation of Tesla's technology at the time.

There are also audio snippets from Jared Birchall, who handles Musk's personal matters. He is heard on a recording of a phone call with online influencer Ashley St. Clair, shortly after she had given birth to a child she and Musk conceived, in which he plays hardball on child support arrangements.

Both incidents were documented in the media: Reuters reported in 2023 on the transcript of Elluswamy's deposition , and The Wall Street Journal reported last year on Birchall's phone call with St. Clair.

But the video and the audio appear to be newly public, giving the documentary a mix of voices beyond the usual critics and creating moments of surprise even for a viewer who is familiar with the ins and outs of Musk's complicated story.

Filmmaker Alex Gibney says in the documentary that he and his team spent more than three years researching Musk, the CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, pulling together not only archival interviews and hard-to-find footage but also a database of quotes from Musk that are peppered throughout the film.

Musk, 55, did not participate in the documentary, and he has panned it, saying on X that it is a " hit piece " and that Gibney has " zero integrity ." Musk, Tesla, SpaceX, Elluswamy and Birchall did not respond to requests for comment.

The nearly four-hour film is a comprehensive tour through Musk's life story, with deep dives into the growth of SpaceX and Tesla, his fathering of 14 known children and his on-again, off-again alliance with President Donald Trump, including his becoming the biggest donor to Trump's 2024 campaign.

The film is a reminder of how often Musk has put himself at the center of public discourse and pop culture, and it moves swiftly through the highlights and lowlights: from his 2021 hosting gig on "Saturday Night Live" and his chaotic purchase of Twitter the next year to his Grok chatbot's embracing the identity " MechaHitler " and his wielding of a chain saw early in Trump's second term.

"I like to call it a 'svelte' four-hour film," producer Jessie Deeter said at a screening Wednesday at the Mill Valley Film Festival in Marin County, California. (The film has a 10-minute intermission, but it is still roughly the length of the 1962 epic "Lawrence of Arabia.")

At the screening, which was about 90% full, the biggest applause came during a moment of anti-Musk defiance, as a former career federal employee explained why they quit the Trump administration last year rather than cooperate with Musk's Department of Government Efficiency.

The film lands at another potentially pivotal moment for Musk, amid speculation that Democrats may investigate him if they take control of Congress after the midterm elections. Polling shows that Musk remains deeply divisive, with a majority of Americans holding unfavorable views of him even as Trump honored him at the White House on Thursday.

The documentary demonstrates that Musk's dabbling in politics is nothing new: Archival videos show that, years before he endorsed Trump in 2024, Musk was rubbing elbows with politicians such as former California Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger, a Republican, and the late Sen. Dianne Feinstein, D-Calif., and getting benefits in return, such as low-emission credits for Tesla .

Part of what drives the documentary forward is how it crosses genres: Parts of it feel like a political thriller or a legal whodunit, while others are like a video game simulation, a science fiction fantasy or a celebrity tabloid drama.

Other moments are closer to a horror film, especially as Gibney narrates some of the graphic details of collisions involving Tesla's driver-assistance software. He includes, for example, dashcam video from a 2019 crash in which a Tesla on "Autopilot" ran a stop sign in Florida and killed a pedestrian — a crash for which a jury found Tesla 33% at fault and ordered it to pay $243 million in damages .

One of the people interviewed in the film, science fiction author and tech activist Cory Doctorow, adds to the grim feeling by wearing a guillotine pin on his lapel.

Later, the documentary lingers again on death, as Gibney tries to tally the human cost of Musk's drive last year to dismantle the U.S. Agency for International Development . Between shots of malnourished children in Africa and elsewhere, Samantha Power, who was a USAID administrator during the Biden administration, says the cuts froze some food programs for the world's poor and blames the cuts for 14 million potential deaths. (The number is based on a projection published last year estimating possible deaths over the following five years.)

In the film's rendering, the horror of those statistics and images stands in stark contrast with Musk's ongoing obsession: traveling deeper into space, including to Mars , for the potential benefit of future, unborn generations.

A few parts of the film are presented without evidence or explanation. Gibney boosts a conspiracy theory that Musk used his Starlink constellation of internet satellites to meddle in the 2024 election — an unfounded idea that independent fact-checkers have long criticized . He also raises concerns about potential data collection by Starlink satellites and by Tesla vehicles but does not go beyond vague theories.

A more pressing question the film wrestles with is whether or how much Musk has changed over his years in the public spotlight. The film repeatedly shows a younger Musk who is not only physically different, with thinner hair and a slighter build, but also speaking about different issues from those he addresses now — including "oil addiction," an old motivation behind growing Tesla.

Another of Musk's associates, former SpaceX engineer Jim Cantrell, says in the film that Musk has changed less than some people may imagine.

"Success has allowed him to take the lid off what he's really thinking," he says.

articles.title: Crazy Rich Asians TV show to reunite Constance Wu and Henry Golding
articles.summary: It will pick up after the hit 2018 film, starring Constance Wu, Henry Golding, Michelle Yeoh and Ronny Chieng.
articles.body:
Four of the stars of 2018's Crazy Rich Asians film are reprising their roles for a TV show of the same name.

The series will pick up events after the end of the hit film, with Constance Wu and Henry Golding playing their lead roles of Rachel and Nick, while Ronny Chieng is back as Eddie and Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh will have a recurring role as Nick's mother Eleanor.

"It's a 'Crazy Rich' family reunion!" said Adele Lim, who co-wrote the film, calling it the sequel we've been waiting for". It will "delve into the characters and worlds of Kevin Kwan's brilliant books" over eight episodes, she said.

The show will be made by HBO, and the news was announced days after HBO's parent company Warner Bros announced its £110bn (£82.8bn) merger with Paramount Skydance .

Adapted from Kwan's bestseller books, written between 2013 and 2017, the film topped the US box office and was nominated for two Golden Globes.

It featured an all-Asian cast and told the story of an Asian-American woman who gets a culture shock meeting her boyfriend's ultra-wealthy family in Singapore.

Lim is showrunner for the new TV series and will be one of the executive producers, as will the the film's director Jon M Chu.

He said the film had "changed his life", calling the cast and crew the "most creative and hilarious group of people I've ever known".

"Since then, this cast has become movie stars, superheroes, arena-filling performers and even an Oscar winner, so bringing everyone back together feels like coming home."

Lim added: "Our writers room is humming and we can't wait to share what we've come up with."

The series, co-produced by HBO and Warner Bros Television, will start production next year.

"Constance, Henry, Ronny, and Michelle are global superstars, and we know the passionate fans of the film and megahit novels can't wait to see more," said said Casey Bloys, co-chair and chief content officer of Skydance Direct-To-Consumer.

articles.summary: El futbolista se ha aliado con American Eagle para lanzar su primera colección de moda: 'American Eagle x Lamine Yamal'
articles.body: El futbolista Lamine Yamal ha llevado su estilo más allá del terreno de juego con la presentación en Barcelona de su primera colección exclusiva junto a American Eagle: 'American Eagle x Lamine Yamal'. La marca estadounidense ha convertido durante 48 horas distintos espacios de la Ciudad Condal en escenarios de una celebración que ha unido moda, música, arte urbano y cultura juvenil para acercar a sus seguidores las 29 prendas diseñadas en colaboración con el jugador del Barça. La iniciativa ha supuesto la primera activación de American Eagle en España y ha formado parte de la estrategia de la compañía para ampliar su presencia y relevancia cultural en Europa. La colección, que se lanzó el mes pasado, ya está disponible a través de la tienda 'online' de la marca. Uno de los principales puntos de encuentro ha sido 'The Studio', un espacio 'pop-up' situado en la Dreta de l’Eixample donde los artistas locales Urees, Otti Hats, Ugo Boulard y Düa Düa impartieron talleres gratuitos de personalización de prendas vaqueras. Los asistentes han podido experimentar con el denim y dar un toque propio a sus prendas, en línea con la apuesta de la colección por la expresión individual. La propuesta también ha llegado al arte urbano con un nuevo mural de 21 metros de altura dedicado a Lamine Yamal y a su colaboración con American Eagle. La obra, creada por el artista TV Boy, se ha convertido en otro de los elementos destacados de la intervención en la ciudad. La celebración ha culminado en el 'American Eagle Beach Club', situado en la playa de Moll de la Marina, donde Lamine Yamal ha hecho una aparición sorpresa. Allí ha ejercido de jurado en una batalla de rap ante cientos de invitados, en un evento que combinó música y cultura urbana. Lamine Yamal se ha mostrado satisfecho con la acogida de la iniciativa y con la posibilidad de compartir el proyecto con su ciudad. "Es muy especial ver cómo mi colección con American Eagle cobra vida aquí, en Barcelona, y cómo la gente hace suyas las prendas", ha declarado el delantero azulgrana, quien también ha destacado su vínculo personal con la moda: "La moda es algo que siempre me ha gustado, y esta colección refleja quién soy y cómo me gusta vestir. Poder compartirla con mi ciudad lo hace aún más especial". Por su parte, Craig Brommers, director de Marketing de American Eagle, ha subrayado la conexión del deportista con las nuevas generaciones y su capacidad para representar los valores de la marca. Según ha exlicado, la colaboración busca unir denim, música, creatividad y cultura juvenil para acercar American Eagle a nuevos consumidores europeos a través de experiencias vinculadas al entorno del futbolista. La colección 'American Eagle x Lamine Yamal', compuesta por 29 prendas, ya se puede adquirir en el sitio web en Europa de la firma estadounidense, en Con esta colaboración, la marca refuerza su apuesta por vincular la moda con figuras del deporte y referentes culturales capaces de conectar con el público joven.

articles.title: In 2025, Mandy Moore found refuge at Hilary Duff’s Beverly Hills home amid Los Angeles wildfires
articles.summary: In January 2025, Mandy Moore sought refuge in Hilary Duff's Beverly Hills home after wildfires devastated her Altadena residence. Both families showed incredible support during the crisis, highlighting the strength of their long-standing friendship.
articles.body: When the devastating Los Angeles wildfires forced Mandy Moore and her family to leave their Altadena home, they found a temporary place to stay with someone they already knew well. Hilary Duff and her husband, Matthew Koma, opened their Beverly Hills home to Moore, her husband Taylor Goldsmith and their three children as the family dealt with the aftermath of the Eaton Fire.The arrangement was revealed by Moore's brother-in-law, Griffin Goldsmith, who also lost his own home in the fires. In an Instagram post shared during the crisis, Griffin thanked Duff and Koma for taking care of his brother's family and for helping his own family through the disaster. People described the gesture as the couple taking in Moore's family after their home was impacted by the fires.How did Mandy Moore's family end up leaving their Altadena home?Moore and Goldsmith had built a family life in Altadena, where they lived with their three children. When the Eaton Fire reached the area in January 2025, the family evacuated with their children and pets.In an Instagram update shared after the evacuation, Mandy Moore explained that the main part of their house was still standing but was unsafe to live in. She also said the garage, home studio and back house had been destroyed, while homes belonging to relatives, friends and neighbours were lost. E! News reported the same details from Moore's social media updates.The situation meant that the family needed somewhere to stay while they figured out what came next. That was when Hilary Duff and Matthew Koma stepped in.Hilary Duff turned her Beverly Hills home into a temporary refugeDuff and Koma offered their Beverly Hills house to Moore, Goldsmith and their children. Griffin Goldsmith publicly expressed his gratitude to the couple, saying they supported his family from the beginning of the crisis.The gesture was especially meaningful because the two actresses have known each other for more than two decades. Architectural Digest noted that Mandy Moore and Hilary Duff had both become well-known young stars in the early 2000s and had remained close as their lives changed and both became mothers.Duff's husband also helped organise a GoFundMe campaign for Griffin and his wife, Kit, whose own home had been destroyed. The fundraiser was intended to help them begin rebuilding after the loss.Inside the Beverly Hills home where Moore's family stayedDuff had a 5,260-square-foot Georgian-style Beverly Hills house that she had transformed into a private family home, according to Architectural Digest. Duff purchased the house after looking for a more secluded place to live. She told the magazine that she liked the feeling of being tucked away from the busy Los Angeles surroundings, describing the property as feeling like a "warm hug."The home had undergone major renovations over the years. Duff worked with designers including David Ko of Maison Ko and the team behind Studio Life/Style to make the interiors brighter and more suitable for family life.That same family-friendly quality became especially relevant when Mandy Moore and her children needed somewhere safe to stay.A friendship that goes beyond HollywoodThe connection between Mandy Moore and Hilary Duff was not simply one between two actors who happened to know each other.The two had remained part of the same social circle as their careers developed and their families grew. Duff had spoken about their close group of mothers and the time they spent together with their children.During the fires, that long friendship took on a very different meaning. Moore's family was dealing with the uncertainty of having a home that could no longer safely accommodate them, while Duff and Koma were able to provide a place where the family could stay.For Moore, the situation was also complicated by the wider loss around her. Her brother-in-law and others close to the family had lost their homes, while much of their Altadena neighbourhood had been badly affected.What happened to Mandy Moore's home later?The damage to Moore's property did not mean the entire house had to be rebuilt from scratch.In a 2026 AD follow-up, Moore and Goldsmith revealed that they had eventually returned to their Altadena home after months of restoration work. The main structure had survived the fire, but smoke damage meant that extensive remediation was necessary.The couple replaced damaged materials, including clothing, textiles and furniture, and undertook work on the home's walls, ductwork and HVAC system before it was considered safe for their children.Their return marked a very different chapter from the early days of the disaster, when Duff's Beverly Hills home had provided a temporary place for the family.From a Hollywood friendship to a real act of supportThe story of Mandy Moore and Hilary Duff during the Los Angeles wildfires became less about celebrity homes and more about what people do for one another when circumstances suddenly change.Moore's family had to leave a house they had spent years making into a home. Duff and Matthew Koma responded by opening their own doors, while also helping another family affected by the fires.Years later, Moore and Goldsmith were able to return to their Altadena home. But for a difficult period when their own house was not safe to live in, Duff's Beverly Hills residence became a temporary home for the family.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: James Bond legend Roger Moore's son calls out TikTok culture, Hollywood's recycled comic book movies
articles.summary: Geoffrey Moore stars in spy thriller "Knightfall" and shares why Hollywood needs stronger stories over big-budget spectacle and recycled comics.
articles.body: Forget bigger explosions — Geoffrey Moore says Hollywood needs better stories. The son of the late James Bond legend Roger Moore told Fox News Digital that today’s films have become too reliant on recycled comic book material and big-budget spectacle, while originality and meaningful dialogue have taken a back seat. "I think that today, it's too much TikTok," the actor told Fox News Digital. "A person will have a conversation with you, and it's the conversation that he read or heard on TikTok, as opposed to actually having read Hemingway and knows what he's talking about." GABRIEL BASSO SAYS SOCIAL MEDIA HAS TURNED PEOPLE INTO VOYEURS OBSESSED WITH STRANGERS' LIVES: 'IT'S WEIRD' "I think it's important that the art of storytelling maintains the culture," Moore said. "There's just too many studio executive heads deciding what's right, as opposed to what people want to hear or people should hear and see." Moore stars in the British spy thriller "Knightfall," which has its share of guns and fight scenes. However, he said the film doesn't rely on over-the-top action to keep audiences hooked and instead leans on a strong storyline and sharp dialogue. "I would like to see more culture in films, as opposed to the regurgitation of these comics," Moore said. WATCH: BOND GIRL ALISON PAPWORTH REVEALS HER HOPE FOR THE NEXT 007 "And everything's so negative. Oh, my goodness. It's like, you need to have a certain budget with helicopters flying upside down. But the storyline has to be strong. Good dialogue, good storywriting are key. You don't have to have constant action to keep the person's attention going. You also need action in the storyline, in the words." Moore also believes "Knightfall" has something else working in its favor in the social media era: It doesn't overstay its welcome. The actor said the film was deliberately kept short, acknowledging that today's audiences may not have the patience to sit through a lengthy saga. "You can't sit through a three-hour movie," he argued. "You can imagine today, it's just everyone on the treadmill. You need that right amount of length before someone starts asking, 'When is it over?' That's the direction I would take with today's films." For Moore, "Knightfall" also marks a full-circle moment. The actor grew up immersed in the entertainment business as the son of one of Hollywood's most famous spies. Now, decades later, he's stepping in front of the camera as a spy himself at roughly the same age his father was when he made his final James Bond film. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "I have not been an actor all my life, even though I did start as a child actor," Moore said. "My second womb was the soundstage. But just because you're related to someone in the entertainment industry, it doesn't make me a part of the entertainment industry or even an actor. But this time, it just felt right. It wasn't forced. And also, it's never too late. I mean, yes, go figure, it's a spy film, but there's a twist. And really, it's never too late." Moore was six years old when his father filmed his 007 debut, "Live and Let Die," which was released in 1973. The Telegraph reported that Moore was present for all of his father's Bond films and the famous stunts that came with them. Once the director yelled "cut," the patriarch would look at his son and ask if he wanted to get ice cream. "Look, I've been on enough film sets to know how laborious it can be," Moore said. "It's a demanding schedule and you mustn't break your ankle. But I've never had a big role where I'm doing a lot of running around. I have to say on some mornings when I wake up, if you've ever been horseback riding, you recognize muscles you never knew you had. I'm doing all of this running around and going, 'Oh my goodness, I thought I was fit!'" "I was never like, 'I'm looking for a job in front of the camera,'" Moore continued. "It just felt right. And I was intrigued. It's an independent British film and very few films aren't dictated by executive heads. This isn't a regurgitation of another franchise where they're spending lots of money. Here, the conditions were harsh. It was physically demanding. Rewrites are happening on the day. It was back to back." "The food was good, considering this wasn't a multimillion production," he said. "And if the money is good, that'll get your attention." Moore said the key to making it in the movie-making business is simple: don't take yourself too seriously. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "If an actor shows up on the set and doesn't understand the importance of the production, what each person does, then they're in the wrong business," he said. "It's a team effort. Everyone is as important. You're nothing without the guy who knows how to keep you in focus. If you make something look good, it's usually not that easy. And to be a film star, you have to be a good actor. There's no such thing as an ignorant person who can act." Despite following in his father's footsteps by playing a spy, Moore isn't campaigning to become the next James Bond. "I think the next James Bond should be someone who can carry the decade, a reflection of the times," Moore said. "When it comes to who's the next Bond, it's really who depicts the times, who is relevant to today, whether it be a tall person, a short person, someone who doesn't know how to tie a tie or who doesn't know how to read because he's on TikTok the whole time. Who knows who they'll choose." "I think they know what they'll be doing. They're not just handing it over to Amazon, that was basically a delivery service, and now they're in the film business. Who they ultimately choose is someone relevant to the times. And I think that's the key to Bond." Amazon MGM Studios gained creative control of the James Bond franchise in 2025 after forming a joint venture with longtime Bond producers Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli. The transaction closed March 24, 2025, with Amazon MGM Studios, Wilson and Broccoli remaining co-owners of the franchise. Several actors have been linked to the role, including Paul Mescal, Jacob Elordi, Jack O'Connell, Jack Lowden and Callum Turner. Denis Villeneuve is set to direct, with "Peaky Blinders" creator Steven Knight writing the screenplay. As Moore looks ahead to making more films, there's one piece of advice from his late father, who died in 2017 at age 89, that he hasn't forgotten. "Make sure you get paid," he joked. articles.title: Zachary Levi says Texas gives him the ‘freedom’ he couldn’t find in California
articles.summary: Zachary Levi says he traded California for Texas "freedom" and values that are "more aligned with mine." The actor is starring in the new Western remake "Angel and the Badman."
articles.body: Zachary Levi believes Texas offered him the kind of freedom and shared values that he no longer felt he had in his home state of California. In 2017, the 45-year-old actor, who is starring in the new Western movie "Angel and the Badman," left Los Angeles behind and moved to a ranch outside Austin. During a recent interview with Fox News Digital alongside his "Angel and the Badman" co-stars, Neal McDonough and Meg Fraser, as well as the film's director, Julio Quintana, Levi reflected on trading the Golden State for the Lone Star State, noting that the "great state of Texas" is a "much easier place to live than a lot of the other places that I have lived." 'FRIDAY NIGHT LIGHTS' STAR ADRIANNE PALICKI SAYS TEXAS GAVE HER SOMETHING HOLLYWOOD COULDN'T "I love California. It's a beautiful state," he said. "Unfortunately, I think it's got a lot of issues and I don't see those going anywhere." "Whereas in Texas, I think that their values are more aligned with mine," he continued. "I appreciate that I don't have to pay state income tax and there's liberty. There's the liberty to go do what I want to go do, which is, like, go buy a bunch of land and build a movie studio." NEWSOM SAYS FILM TAX INCENTIVES ARE BRINGING HOLLYWOOD HOME BUT INDUSTRY EXPERTS WARN IT MAY BE 'TOO LATE' "You can be a crazy person and go do that," Levi added. "If Walt Disney tried to go build Disneyland in California today, I don't think it would ever get done, you know, so it gives me the freedom to go live the life that I believe that I'm meant to go live." Levi is currently building Wyldwood Studios, a $100 million film and lifestyle campus on his 75-acre property in Bastrop County outside Austin. Designed as a hybrid production hub and creative retreat, the multiphase project pairs soundstages and production offices with housing and wellness spaces. Wyldwood is expected to open its first two soundstages in 2027. WATCH: ZACHARY LEVI SAYS TEXAS GAVE HIM THE FREEDOM HE COULDN'T FIND IN CALIFORNIA The "Chuck" alum previously told Fox News Digital that the inspiration to build Wyldwood was rooted in his longstanding desire to rethink how the entertainment industry operates from the inside out. "Ever since I started working in Hollywood and I saw how broken it all was, I felt very compelled by God to go build a better Hollywood — like a new United Artists kind of studio — where it's owned and operated by the artists, where we can cut out all the middlemen, where we all can do really well, build a community," Levi said. "And then not just a place to work," he continued. "People can live there, and kids can go to school there. And we have an organic farm, and, like, all of the things that I think everybody really wants these days." Levi's latest project, "Angel and the Badman," which was produced by Angel Studios, is a remake of the classic 1947 Western of the same name that starred John Wayne, Gail Russell, Harry Carey and Bruce Cabot. The official plot synopsis for the remake reads, "When feared outlaw Quirt Evans staggers onto a rancher's land with a bullet in his back, he expects a quick death, not mercy. But Penny, the rancher's daughter, offers him a chance at something he’s never had: a life beyond violence. However, the past doesn’t forgive. With the marshal closing in and an outlaw gang ready to burn the ranch to the ground, Quirt must decide what kind of man he’ll be when the world demands blood." Levi stepped into Wayne's original role as Quirt Evans (the Badman) while Fraser plays Penny (the Angel) and McDonough portrays the marshal. "Angel and the Badman" also stars Tommy Lee Jones as the outlaw gang leader Laredo. WATCH: NEAL MCDONOUGH SAYS YOUNG PEOPLE NEED TO SEE ‘THE BAD GUY GETS WHAT HE DESERVES’ While speaking with Fox News Digital, McDonough explained how he believes "Angel and the Badman" conveys an important message for the young people of today. "I think nowadays — with the temptation of social media and what we look at and what we hear and what we listen to — who do we look up to as heroes anymore?" he said. "Especially for the younger generation, it's really hard for them." "The younger generation who don't really know Westerns so well, to go to a film like ‘Angel and the Badman,’ you see, ‘OK, the bad guy gets what he deserves in the end,’" McDonough continued. "Where in modern day, the bad guy sometimes gets to go scot-free and that's tough to really learn from as a kid. What do you learn from that as a young adult?" "So films like this are important because it tells us, you should be trying to do the right thing," he added. "You should redeem yourself and not do the dumb things that you used to do. Try to be a better person, try to give glory to Him, try and do the right thing for your family. I love doing films like these because they do exactly that, and thank goodness for Angel Studios." Quintana said he believed that the story’s redemptive themes feel especially relevant in a social media era when public mistakes can quickly become permanent scandals. "In modern culture, in some ways, we actually have the inverse situation where it seems like we're always — you make one public mistake, and it's like your life is ruined," he said. "Our media outlets thrive on downfall and self-destruction and things like that. And I think this is a good reminder that actually what's really inspiring is people making mistakes and ultimately making the sacrifices to make amends and try to claw their way back up and try to be better, because we don't really see the redemptive side of a public downfall. articles.title: In 2023, Heather Dubrow bought a Beverly Hills mansion for $16 million; renovations pushed the projected cost to $32 million
articles.summary: Explore the expensive journey of Heather Dubrow as she navigates her ambitious $32 million renovation of a Beverly Hills mansion purchased for $16 million. Learn about the challenges, financial burdens, and the eventual sale of this dream home gone wrong.
articles.body: For Heather Dubrow, buying a Beverly Hills mansion was supposed to be another dream house project. She and her husband, Dr. Terry Dubrow, had already built and sold their famous Orange County home, so their next property was meant to be something special too.They bought the Beverly Hills estate in 2023 for around $16 million. Then came the renovation plans. Heather wanted to take the house “down to the studs,” and the projected all-in cost eventually reached around $32 million. What looked like an exciting new chapter slowly turned into a very expensive headache.Heather Dubrow bought the Beverly Hills estate for $16.1 million in 2023On 24 July 2023, Entertainment Tonight reported that Heather and Terry Dubrow had bought the Beverly Hills property for $16.1 million, well below its original $37.5 million asking price. Heather herself confirmed the purchase to ET and called it an “iconic, Hollywood estate.”The estate had a serious Hollywood connection. It had previously belonged to legendary film producer Dino De Laurentiis and his wife, producer Martha De Laurentiis. The property sits in the Beverly Hills Post Office area, at the end of a long gated driveway.The estate also gave the Dubrows plenty to work with. It had expansive grounds, a swimming pool, a tennis court, multiple living spaces and views stretching across Los Angeles.Heather Dubrow wanted to completely transform the Beverly Hills mansionThe house was never supposed to stay the way they bought it. During the Season 18 premiere of 'The Real Housewives of Orange County' on 11 July 2024, Heather Dubrow explained just how ambitious the renovation was. She said they were going to take the house “down to the studs,” essentially stripping it back before rebuilding it around her vision.But there was a slightly funny reality to all that planning: they were already living in the house while figuring everything out.Heather showed viewers rooms with temporary furniture and even a refrigerator marked “do not open.” She joked about how strange it was to be living in the middle of a future construction site.Heather Dubrow's $32 million renovation was a projection, not a final billThis is where the numbers around the Beverly Hills mansion can get confusing. The $32 million figure was a projected running total, not an amount Heather and Terry Dubrow were confirmed to have spent.In the July 2024 episode, the couple's renovation planning estimated that they could spend around $2 million to $3 million on landscaping, more than $2 million on the guest house and another $1 million on a movie theater. Along with the other work, that pushed the projected total cost of the property to around $32 million.Heather Dubrow later spoke directly to Bravo on 6 August 2024 about the project, describing the house as very different from her previous homes. At that stage, the estimated running total was still around $32 million.So, technically, Heather and Terry did not buy a $32 million house. They bought it for roughly $16 million and were looking at a potential $32 million all-in cost after the planned renovation.Heather Dubrow's dream renovation turned into a financial burdenThe renovation became much more complicated than Heather Dubrow had expected. By the time the Dubrows were discussing the project again on 'RHOC', the house had become a major source of stress. Heather later described the construction as a “disaster,” while the couple faced delays, rising costs and major work on the property.The situation became even more complicated when asbestos was discovered during the renovation. Heather also revealed that the contractor had gone significantly over the budget they had originally agreed upon. What was meant to be a dream home was now a house that required even more time and money.Heather Dubrow eventually sold the Beverly Hills mansion for $16.5 millionBy 2025, the Dubrows decided it was time to let the property go. The Beverly Hills estate was listed for $25 million in March 2025 and was later reduced to just under $20 million. The property ultimately sold for $16.5 million in August 2025, according to The Real Deal's contemporaneous report on the transaction.Heather Dubrow later admitted that walking away from the project was difficult. In Bravo's coverage of the sale, she described it as a project she had once seen as her dream house but eventually realised was not viable for the family anymore.And that is what makes the Beverly Hills mansion story so striking. Heather Dubrow went into the deal thinking she had found another home to put her personal stamp on. Instead, a roughly $16 million purchase came with a projected $32 million renovation, construction problems and a $16.5 million sale two years later.Sometimes, even in Beverly Hills, the dream house is the one you eventually decide to leave behind.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: At 13, Jason Weaver was offered $2 million by Disney to sing as young Simba in The Lion King; his mother chose $100,000 plus royalties instead, and 32 years later he says the checks are still coming
articles.summary: At 13, most children are still figuring out what they want to be when they grow up.
articles.body: At 13, most children are still figuring out what they want to be when they grow up. For Jason Weaver, however, life had already presented an opportunity that could have changed his family's fortunes overnight. When Disney offered him $2 million to lend his voice to young Simba in The Lion King, it was the kind of money most teenagers could only dream of. But his mother and manager, Marilyn “Kitty” Haywood, saw something beyond the staggering figure. She turned down the lump-sum offer, negotiated an upfront payment of around $100,000 and royalties instead, and made a decision that Weaver says continues to pay off more than three decades later.Now 47, the actor and singer has revealed how his mother's foresight helped him build a lasting source of income from one of Disney's most successful animated films. Recalling the deal in a 2019 interview with VladTV, which has recently resurfaced on social media, Weaver said the original offer was essentially designed to pay him once and close the matter.“When they offered that deal, it was really just to take this money and go,” he recalled, suggesting that Disney already anticipated the enormous commercial potential of the film.For a family from Chicago, $2 million in the early 1990s was no small amount. Weaver had already experienced success, including playing a young Michael Jackson, for which he said his biggest cheque until then had been around $80,000. The Disney offer was therefore a life-changing sum by any ordinary measure. Yet his mother understood that the value of the opportunity might extend far beyond what was being offered upfront.Why his mother turned down $2 millionHaywood, who had experience in the music industry as a singer with the Chicago group Kitty & the Haywoods and as a backing vocalist for Aretha Franklin, was not easily swayed by a large cheque. She understood that entertainment contracts could have consequences lasting years, and she wanted her son to benefit if the film continued to generate revenue long after its theatrical release.Her thinking was rooted in Disney's own history. The studio had repeatedly brought its classic animated films back to audiences through re-releases, allowing them to find new generations of viewers. With Aladdin and Beauty and the Beast having already established the commercial strength of Disney's animated revival, she had reason to believe that The Lion King could enjoy a similarly long life.As Weaver explained, his mother looked beyond the immediate payout and considered what the film might mean for him decades later.“She was able to see the playing field and go, wait a minute, this is gonna make a lot of money over time, so what happens when my son turns 40? Is he still gonna be able to get a check from this when they eventually release this?” he recalled. “And sure enough, she was absolutely right.”Instead of accepting the $2 million outright, Haywood negotiated an upfront payment of approximately $100,000 along with royalties. It was a gamble that required patience and a willingness to bet on the film's future success rather than take a guaranteed fortune in the present.The gamble that kept paying off for more than three decadesThe decision was not without risk. Weaver has said that royalty arrangements were not routinely offered to newcomers at the time, with such deals more commonly associated with established stars. His mother's industry experience, however, gave her the confidence to negotiate rather than simply accept Disney's first proposal.The scale of The Lion King's success ultimately made that decision particularly rewarding. What began as an animated feature grew into a global entertainment franchise, spanning merchandise, video games, stage productions, theme park attractions and subsequent screen adaptations.Weaver has pointed to the enormous sums generated by the franchise over the years, observing that the money Disney made from it could run into hundreds of millions, if not billions, of dollars. Against that backdrop, the original $2 million offer began to look less like an extraordinary windfall and more like a one-time payment that could have cost him years of earnings.The actor has said that he has since earned more through the arrangement than the amount Disney initially offered. He has not publicly disclosed the total royalties he has received or the precise amount of his recurring payments, but he continues to describe the income as a welcome source of financial security.In fact, the first royalty cheque was so unexpected that even Weaver and his mother initially questioned whether it was correct.“When I got my first royalty check, me and my mom thought it was a mistake,” he said.That disbelief has given way to appreciation over the years. For Weaver, the payments are a reminder of a decision made when he was too young to fully understand the financial implications of the opportunity in front of him.‘I wasn't thinking about a portfolio’Looking back, Weaver has also acknowledged that receiving $2 million at 13 might not necessarily have led to the same long-term outcome. As a teenager, he was unlikely to have been thinking about investments, financial planning or ways to preserve a fortune over several decades.“I wasn’t thinking about a portfolio, or diversifying,” he said.His mother's decision, therefore, did more than secure a potential stream of future earnings. It also protected him from the possibility of receiving an enormous sum at an age when managing it responsibly would have been a challenge.The continuing royalties have proved particularly valuable because they are not dependent on whether he is currently working on a film, television show or music project. As Weaver put it, the residual income remains helpful even today.“Honestly that income, that residual income that I generate—man that is so helpful,” he said. “Even nowadays, when I get a check, it’s like...yes!”The arrangement also has implications for the next generation. Weaver has said that he agreed to terms allowing the royalties to pass down to his children and potentially their descendants, extending the benefits of his mother's decision well beyond his own career.From young Simba to a career across television, film and musicWhile The Lion King remains one of the defining achievements of Weaver's early career, it was far from his last major professional milestone. After voicing young Simba and singing on the film's soundtrack, he went on to establish himself as an actor in both television and cinema.He appeared in the sitcom Thea from 1993 to 1994 before taking on the role of Marcus Henderson in Smart Guy, which ran from 1997 to 1999. His film credits include Drumline, The Ladykillers and ATL. In more recent years, he has appeared in television series including The Chi and Sistas.Music remained an important part of his journey, too. Weaver released his debut album, Love Ambition, through Motown in 1995. In 2004, he featured on Chingy's single “One Call Away”, which reached No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100.His career has therefore extended well beyond the Disney classic, but the financial benefits of his work on The Lion King continue to occupy a special place in his story.A decision that turned a childhood opportunity into a lasting legacyThe success of The Lion King has only reinforced the wisdom of Haywood's decision. The original animated film became a global box-office phenomenon, while the 2019 photorealistic remake went on to earn more than $1.6 billion worldwide. The franchise's continuing popularity has helped keep the story relevant to new generations of audiences.Online estimates have placed Weaver's net worth between $4 million and $7 million, although those figures have not been independently confirmed. More importantly, the actor himself has made clear that the royalties have continued to provide meaningful financial support throughout his adult life.There is also something deeply personal about the story. At 13, Weaver was the face, or, more accurately, the voice, of a character who would become a beloved part of popular culture. He could not have been expected to predict the franchise's extraordinary longevity. His mother, however, recognised that a successful film could become an enduring asset rather than a single paycheque.More than 30 years later, the result is a reminder that the biggest financial decision is not always about how much money arrives today, but how much value an opportunity can create over time.For Weaver, the $2 million Disney offer might once have seemed like a dream come true. Instead, his mother's willingness to look beyond it helped turn a childhood role into a source of income that continues to surprise him, and one that may benefit his family for generations to come.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Traitors' Celia Imrie and Wiltshire's Fidelis Morgan travel world
articles.summary: Celia Imrie and Wiltshire actress Fedilis Morgan will be talking about their new book at the event.
articles.body:
A Wiltshire writer and actress has said travelling the world with Celebrity Traitors star Celia Imrie is "easy" because they are very well-matched companions.

Fidelis Morgan is not only friends with Imrie but is also collaborating with her on a book called "The Elegant Hustler: Adventures From a Life on the Move". The pair will be discussing it at the Cheltenham Literature Festival.

Imrie, 74 - who has starred in shows from Dinnerladies to the Bridget Jones films and more recently the Celebrity Traitors - said she was "so happy" the "extraordinary" BBC hit series had given her new generations of young fans.

Morgan said Traitors was a "very early lesson in psychology" for young people.

The pair, who met in 1975 while working for The Royal Shakespeare Company, said it was there they realised they both "adored travelling" and could have fun together on the way

The pair have been travelling the world by train, ship and plane and documenting their adventures along the way

The duo said it was their preference to travel by sea and rail and avoid flying if possible.

"I had two pulmonary embolisms and the doctor said best not [fly] if you can avoid it and I'm very happy to avoid airports," Imrie said.

Morgan added: "You see things in American trains that you would never see if you drove or if you flew.

"We've seen the wildest of animals - alligators and roadrunners, bears, orange pigs - and eagles."

articles.summary: Katie Price’s former husband Kieran Hayler allegedly told a 13-year-old girl who has accused him of rape that she could be his “best friend” because he
articles.body: Katie Price’s former husband Kieran Hayler allegedly told a 13-year-old girl who has accused him of rape that she could be his “best friend” because he had no friends of his own, a court has heard. The allegation emerged during Hayler’s trial at Lewes Crown Court in East Sussex, where he denies three counts of rape and one count of sexual assault involving the complainant, who is now 23.According to The Sun, the girl’s mother, while giving evidence, told the jury that her daughter had liked the way Hayler spoke to her. Recalling what her daughter had allegedly told her, the mother said, “She said he told her he didn't have any friends and she could be his best friend.”“She liked the way he spoke to her,” she added.The allegations relate to incidents said to have taken place in West Sussex between June 1 and October 13, 2016. Hayler, 39, denies all the charges against him, and the case is continuing.Mother says she wanted to protect her daughter’s trustThe court also heard why the complainant’s mother did not disclose the allegations to others until after Katie Price contacted social services in 2018. Asked about the delay, the mother said she had wanted to preserve her daughter’s trust and keep what she had been told confidential.“I had to keep her secret and her trust,” she told the court.“I couldn't tell my husband because I knew what the consequences would be. I didn't want any of this for her.”The mother denied that Katie Price had influenced her decision to attend court or give evidence. She also rejected suggestions that her daughter was interested in becoming a celebrity.During the proceedings, the jury heard about text messages exchanged between Price and the complainant, in which the reality television personality allegedly offered to make the young woman a “little star”. The messages were read out to the mother during her evidence.Defence barrister Arlette Piercy questioned the mother about the exchange and what she knew about the allegations. The witness maintained that her daughter had not been motivated by the prospect of fame.“My daughter wasn't interested in becoming a star,” she said.When challenged over whether she had believed that anything had happened and whether she had taken action, the mother replied, “Yes, I did. I believed my daughter.”Defence claims allegations were part of a campaign against HaylerThe trial has also heard that Hayler believes he is being set up by his former wife following the breakdown of their marriage. When proceedings opened, jurors were told that he would argue the allegations had been fabricated as part of a campaign against him.The complainant’s mother firmly denied that anyone had pressured or influenced her to come forward or give evidence against Hayler.Crown prosecutor Ryan Richter asked her whether she had attended court to support her daughter by making up the allegations. She replied, “No, I have not.”Asked whether anybody had influenced or pressured her to make the claims, she said, “No, nobody.”The mother also told the court that she had attended forgiveness counselling with a kinesiology therapist. She explained that, alongside treatment relating to her arthritis, the therapist also practised what she described as psychic healing.Complainant allegedly received ‘I love you’ text after third incidentEarlier in the trial, the complainant gave evidence about the alleged incidents and told jurors that Hayler had sent her a text message after the third alleged rape, saying, “I love you goodnight.”She said she had replied, “I love you too.”The complainant contacted the NSPCC in 2021, and the charity referred the matter to the police, prompting an investigation. Hayler was first interviewed by police in January 2022, when he denied the allegations and denied that anything sexual had taken place.Sussex Police previously confirmed that Hayler had been charged with three counts of rape and one count of sexual assault involving a girl aged 13 at the time of the alleged offences. The complainant cannot be named for legal reasons and has received support from specially trained officers.Katie Price expected to give evidence during the trialJurors have also been told that Katie Price, the mother of five and a prominent media personality, is expected to be called as a witness during the proceedings. Judge Mark Van Der Zwart described Price as a media personality whom the jury had likely heard of.Hayler met Price in 2012 and proposed to her on Christmas Day that year. The couple married at a luxury resort in the Caribbean in 2013 before their relationship eventually ended.Hayler has consistently denied the allegations. In a previous statement, a representative for him said he “strongly denies the allegations made against him in their entirety”, adding that he had cooperated with the police investigation and looked forward to clearing his name through the judicial process.The trial at Lewes Crown Court is ongoing. The allegations remain unproven, and Hayler is entitled to the presumption of innocence unless and until he is found guilty.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Ed Sheeran’s New U.S. Loop Tour Opening Acts Revealed After Macklemore Controversy
articles.summary: Isaac Slade of The Fray and Brooks Rosser of ‘American Idol’ announced they’ll join Sheeran at upcoming dates of his ongoing Loop Tour
articles.body:
Isaac Slade will open four of Ed Sheeran's U.S. Loop Tour shows, beginning Oct. 10 in Indianapolis

American Idol finalist Brooks Rosser joins Slade for the Indianapolis concert

Macklemore was removed as an opening act after venue owners objected to his comments supporting Palestinians

Who is the opening act for the rest of Ed Sheeran 's U.S. Loop Tour dates?

On Thursday, Oct. 8, Isaac Slade of The Fray and Brooks Rosser of American Idol announced they'll join Sheeran, 35, for some of his remaining Loop Tour dates in North America after Macklemore was previously removed from the shows following his onstage comments in support of Palestine.

Slade, 45, took to Instagram and shared that he'll open four of Sheeran's upcoming shows: Oct. 10 at the Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Oct. 17 at the Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C., Oct. 24 at the AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, and Nov. 7 at the Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Fla.

"See you out there," wrote the "How to Save a life" singer, who fronted The Fray from the band's 2002 inception through his departure in 2022.

Rosser, 23, who made it to the top 7 on season 24 of American Idol , announced he'll join Sheeran and Slade for the Indianapolis concert. "my first show since American Idol, and it's at Lucas Oil Stadium opening for @teddysphotos ," he wrote on Instagram . "I'm beyond excited and grateful. See you Saturday!"

Sheeran's Oct. 29 and Oct. 30 shows at Hard Rock Live in Hollywood, Fla., still feature no opening acts.

On Sept. 14, Macklemore revealed he was removed as an opening act on the Loop Tour. He revealed the "Shape of You" singer told him Robert Kraft, who owns Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Mass., said the "Thrift Shop" rapper would not be allowed to perform at the venue for his scheduled tour stops with Sheeran due to his political comments.

"Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues," wrote Macklemore, whose real name is Benjamin Haggerty.

Sheeran later confirmed the information in his own statement , noting he spoke with Kraft in an attempt to "build a bridge," but "the venue's and promoter's decision was final."

Kraft told PEOPLE in a statement at the time that Gillette does not "provide a platform for hate speech."

Macklemore later donated $1 million in earnings from Sheeran's tour to Palestinian relief organizations. He also launched the three-date Free Palestine tour , which he said "sold out immediately." Kraft, meanwhile, said Sheeran asked him to match a $2 million donation to humanitarian aid in the area.

All of Sheeran's opening acts and his backing band dropped out of the Loop Tour in solidarity with Macklemore. The two shows Sheeran was set to perform at Gillette were ultimately canceled due to a nor'easter.

Slade first joined Sheeran as an opening act on the Loop Tour on Oct. 3 at the Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta. "Everybody seems to be taking sides in this world and that's good," Slade said on stage, according to Billboard . "What's happening over there [in Gaza] is wrong but if we're going to get through it, we're going to need people to step into that middle place, that common ground."

articles.title: Kamal Haasan STRONGLY responds to Elon Musk’s Starlink claim: 'India is a democracy, not a colony'; says the country will decide its own future
articles.summary: Kamal Haasan has responded to Elon Musk’s allegations about Starlink’s delayed entry into India.
articles.body: Kamal Haasan has responded to Elon Musk’s allegations about Starlink’s delayed entry into India. The SpaceX CEO had claimed that the satellite internet company was being held back by powerful business interests. Now, the veteran actor shared his reply on X on Friday, saying India will decide its own future.What Elon Musk allegedElon Musk said on Wednesday that Starlink was “blocked by certain oligarchs” in India to protect their “monopolistic chokehold” over the country. He added that the company is licensed in more than 165 countries and had spent five years complying with Indian laws and government requirements. "So why still no license?" he asked. "Is Ambani the real boss of India?" he added.Kamal Haasan’s reply on competitionKamal Haasan, who represents Tamil Nadu in the Rajya Sabha, began, "Mr. Musk, yes, no billionaire should dictate a nation’s policy – Indian or American India must welcome competition in satellite internet from Indian and global providers, whoever offers the most practical and affordable last-mile solution for those in remote regions. In countries with lower per-capita incomes, satellite internet must be affordable too. High subscription fees and equipment costs risk putting it beyond the reach of ordinary households. Connectivity must bridge the digital divide, not create a new one.”National security and double standardsHe added, "India knows our networks and spectrum are strategic infrastructure, not merely commercial assets. India’s national security safeguards are non-negotiable.Every country makes choices based on its own interests. Those in the West cannot preach free markets while practising protectionism at home. USA imposed 100% tariffs on Chinese EVs to protect its domestic industry, just as India takes measures to protect its own domestic manufacturers. Both India and the US have restricted Huawei over security concerns. One cannot demand a level playing field from others only when it suits its own agenda."Kamal Haasan says, 'We, Indian people, will decide our own future'Kamal Haasan also pointed to the BharatNet programme, saying, “We will question why, as the CAG’s 2026 audit report found, the programme is struggling to meet its original objectives. Why were only 33.2% of service-ready Gram Panchayats operational, despite Rs 39,888 crore being spent? articles.body: “Pretty Little Liars” actor Keegan Allen was mugged in the parking lot of a West Hollywood grocery store by two masked men who beat him up and stole his watch, the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department said Friday. In the aftermath of the Thursday evening attack, Allen posted video of himself with blood on his face and his left arm. “I was just, I was just robbed of my watch outside of Laurel Supply,” the rattled actor can be heard saying. “Can you call the police?” Allen, who is 37, also gave his account of what happened. “But these two dudes hit me in the head and pointed a gun at me with, with a knife, and then took off,” Allen said in the footage. “I ah — They had masks on.” “Took my watch, though,” he added. “Damn it! “ Allen, according to investigators, had just returned to his vehicle from the upscale grocery store on Santa Monica Boulevard when he was confronted by two men. “One suspect pointed a silver handgun at the victim while the other pointed a knife and demanded the victim’s watch and bracelet,” the sheriff’s department said in a statement. “Shortly after, the victim was struck in the face with the handgun. The suspects obtained the victim’s watch and fled the scene in an unknown vehicle.” Allen “sustained a laceration to his forehead” but was not hospitalized, the department said, adding that they are “actively investigating this incident” and additional patrols will sent to the area. In the caption to his Instagram post, Allen wrote, “West Hollywood is not safe anymore.” “Robbed at gunpoint and knifepoint by two young men that threatened to KILL me over my watch and would have! God said no tonight. My life for a watch,” he wrote. He then called out Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass and California Gov. Gavin Newsom, writing, “Let’s hope all these flock cameras ... everyone thinks will stop crime can find these very dangerous criminals.” The city of West Hollywood released a statement in response to the incident, insisting it is “a compassionate and engaged community.” “The City wants community members to know that community concerns are heard and taken seriously, and that public safety remains the City’s top priority,” the statement said.
