articles.standfirst: La DJ, que pasó siete meses hospitalizada y recibió quimioterapia y un trasplante de médula, ha anunciado que los médicos le han detectado un nuevo linfoma meses después de regresar a los escenarios
articles.summary: La DJ, que pasó siete meses hospitalizada y recibió quimioterapia y un trasplante de médula, ha anunciado que los médicos le han detectado un nuevo linfoma meses después de regresar a los escenarios
articles.body: La DJ española Beatriz Martínez, conocida artísticamente como B Jones, ha anunciado que le han detectado un nuevo linfoma, poco después de compartir con sus seguidores que había vencido al cáncer. La artista ha comunicado la noticia a través de una publicación en Instagram en la que ha explicado el impacto emocional que supone afrontar este nuevo diagnóstico después de meses de tratamiento y de empezar a pensar en una nueva etapa de su vida. "Hace poco compartí con vosotros una de las noticias más felices de mi vida: había vencido al cáncer", comienza el comunicado de la DJ, que recuerda el largo proceso que ha atravesado para recuperarse. Después de someterse a meses de quimioterapia y un trasplante de médula, creía que había dejado atrás la enfermedad y que podía comenzar a recuperar la normalidad. Sin embargo, poco después recibió una nueva noticia médica. "La vida volvió a darme un golpe: un nuevo linfoma, esta vez en otra zona de la cabeza", ha explicado B Jones. La artista ha reconocido que asimilar la noticia está siendo especialmente difícil después de todo lo vivido y de la esperanza que había depositado en su recuperación. "Aceptar que todo esto aún no había terminado, después de haber pasado por tanto y de creer que por fin podía empezar a recuperarme, está siendo increíblemente duro", ha confesado. En su mensaje, B Jones no ha ocultado la dificultad de afrontar esta nueva situación, aunque ha asegurado que está intentando reunir fuerzas para hacer frente a esta etapa. "Aquí estoy, asimilándolo y reuniendo fuerzas para afrontar una nueva batalla", ha escrito. La DJ también ha querido transmitir un mensaje de esperanza, sin restar importancia a la dureza del momento que atraviesa. "No voy a decir que es fácil, porque no lo es. Pero sigo teniendo esperanza, ganas de vivir y mucho por lo que luchar", ha afirmado. El comunicado termina con unas palabras que reflejan su determinación ante el nuevo diagnóstico: "Toca volver a empezar. Una vez más. Porque esta historia todavía no ha terminado". La publicación, acompañada de varias fotografías desde la cama del hospital, ha recibido numerosas muestras de apoyo y mensajes de ánimo por parte de sus seguidores. La noticia llega después de que B Jones protagonizara uno de los momentos más significativos de su recuperación. El pasado mes de julio, la artista regresó al Mainstage de Tomorrowland después de meses alejada de los escenarios por la enfermedad, cumpliendo así su promesa de volver a actuar en uno de los festivales de música electrónica más importantes del mundo. Durante su lucha contra el cáncer, la DJ pasó siete meses hospitalizada y afrontó un largo proceso de tratamiento y recuperación. Su regreso a Tomorrowland estuvo marcado por una emotiva introducción con un mensaje de esperanza y perseverancia. Debido a las secuelas del tratamiento, su actuación fue más corta y la organización adaptó la cabina para que pudiera pinchar desde su silla de ruedas. La actuación supuso un hito en su vuelta a la música después de una etapa en la que había evitado fijar fechas para regresar a los escenarios y había centrado sus esfuerzos en recuperarse. Ahora, ¡después de haber compartido que había superado el cáncer, B Jones afronta un nuevo diagnóstico de linfoma. La artista ha hecho pública la noticia mientras intenta asimilar lo ocurrido y reunir fuerzas para afrontar esta nueva etapa.

articles.title: Ella Langley cancels Tulsa concert after false bomb threat
articles.summary: The country singer shared a statement on Instagram apologizing to fans and explaining why the Oct. 9 show in Oklahoma, was canceled.
articles.body:
This story has been updated to include a statement from the Tulsa Police Department.

Country singer Ella Langley canceled her Oct. 9 concert at the BOK Center in Tulsa, Okla., following a security threat, telling fans she refused to put anyone in danger.

"Due to a serious security threat involving the safety of my fans, the venue staff, and my team, the incredibly difficult decision was made to cancel tonight's show," Langley wrote on Instagram . "This decision was made under the advisement of local authorities, the venue, and my security team."

Tulsa Police Department Capt. Richard Meulenberg said in a video posted to Facebook that officers conducted multiple security sweeps of the BOK Center, including searches with bomb-sniffing dogs. The initial searches found no threat, but police returned after receiving a phone call warning of potential gunfire and bombs at the event.

"We came out again in an overabundance of caution, used our bomb dogs again, searched the entire area," Meulenberg said. "We could not find a credible threat here at the BOK Center."

Meulenberg emphasized that neither the police department nor the venue canceled the concert. He said officers informed Langley's team that they had found no credible threat and left the decision to proceed with the performance to the artist's team.

"We advised the group that was supposed to be performing tonight that we could not find a credible threat," Meulenberg said. "We would never tell anybody, if we couldn't find a credible threat, to cancel their event. So they made the decision to cancel their event tonight."

The police captain expressed disappointment for the thousands of concertgoers affected by the cancellation.

"The most disappointing thing is that thousands of people were here for this long-awaited event to come and enjoy the show, and they can't be here," Meulenberg said. "So the person who called us in with a phone call disrupted this entire event for all these folks."

Langley was scheduled to perform at the 19,199-seat venue with special guests Kameron Marlowe and Laci Kaye Booth . The venue shared the same statement confirming the cancellation and said additional information about ticket refunds would be shared as soon as possible. No rescheduled date for the Tulsa concert had been announced.

"I know how much time, travel, money, and planning goes into coming to a show, and I can't tell you how sorry I am," Langley wrote. "This is not a decision that was made lightly. I was so looking forward to spending tonight with you, but your safety will always mean more to me than anything else. I refuse to put anyone in harm's way."

The "Dandelion" singer's next performance is Oct. 10 at United Supermarkets Arena in Lubbock, Texas, also with Marlowe and Booth. No cancellation of that performance has been announced.

articles.title: Hayden Panettiere's ex-fiancé Wladimir Klitschko granted temporary guardianship of her estate
articles.summary: Wladimir Klitschko appeared in virtual court on Thursday alongside 11-year-old daughter Kaya, who he shares alongside Panettiere. Kaya is the sole heir of th...
articles.body:
Hayden Panettiere's former fiancé, Wladimir Klitschko, was granted temporary guardianship of her estate on Friday, following the actor's sudden death in August.

Klitschko appeared in virtual court on Thursday alongside their 11-year-old daughter Kaya, according to People .

Kaya is the sole heir of the estate of the "Heroes" star, who on Aug. 16 was found unresponsive in a Greenville, S.C., residence. The Greenville County Coroner's Office ruled the death an accidental overdose involving several drugs, including fentanyl.

Klitschko filed a petition in a Los Angeles County court on Sept. 24, requesting that he be allowed to act as Kaya's representative. The Ukrainian boxer and Olympic gold medalist has had full custody of their daughter since 2018.

The filing cites items that were seized from her home in a federal investigation with no assurance that they will be returned, as well as unauthorized people who gained access to her Los Angeles residence.

"Without an immediate appointment for these purposes, there is a high probability that property belonging to Hayden's Estate may be lost, damaged or dissipated before a duly appointed personal representative can be in place to protect it," the filing stated.

According to the petition, Panettiere and Klitschko hired security before her death to protect her home because an unnamed person gained access inside. Her ex-fiancé feared that the same person would continue to "misappropriate" items belonging to the actor's estate.

A day before their Oct. 8 court date, Klitschko submitted a supplemental claim to the earlier petition where he believed someone from outside of Panettiere's family was selling some of her possessions, including jewelry, to a pawn shop, per ABC News .

In addition to seeking guardianship, Klitschko also asked the courts to grant him the ability to "request and authorize law enforcement investigation into the recovery of Hayden's property believed to have been misappropriated."

Panettiere and Klitschko had an on-and-off relationship between 2009 and 2018 and were briefly engaged in 2013. In 2014, the "Nashville" and "Ice Princess" star welcomed their daughter, but relinquished full custody to Klitschko in 2018 due to her struggles with postpartum depression and substance abuse.

"It was the hardest thing I could do," she said during a 2022 appearance on "Red Table Talk." "But the best thing for my daughter was to make sure she was OK, take care of myself and make sure I could be a good mom to her. And sometimes that means letting go."

Klitschko has always spoken highly of Panettiere, lamenting his loss on Instagram, where he shared a picture of the two with Kaya (with an orange dot covering her face) on Aug. 18 . In his post, he stated that the family was going through "profound shock and grief." He also acknowledged his ex-fiancé's experience navigating demands of the entertainment industry.

"Nothing will erase the times we shared or the place she had in our lives," he wrote in the Instagram caption . "To our daughter Kaya, I will always speak of her mother with respect and make sure she remembers the person she was."

The next hearing is scheduled for Dec. 7, when permanent guardianship of the estate will be decided; however Kaya does not need to be present.

Times staff writer Alexandra Del Rosario contributed to this report.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Hollywood feeling more hopeful amid a push for film tax credits and Paramount staying put, filmmaker says
articles.summary: California expands its film and television tax credits and launches a post-production incentive as Hollywood fights to keep jobs in Los Angeles.
articles.body: Now that Paramount is staying put in Los Angeles and state and federal lawmakers are pushing for expanded film tax credits, Hollywood insiders are seeing a glimmer of hope. On Wednesday, California Gov. Gavin Newsom highlighted the state’s latest efforts to bolster its entertainment industry, including a new post-production tax credit, an expanded film and television tax credit and new protections for performers against the use of AI-generated content. "California is the home of entertainment, full stop," Newsom said in a statement. "We’re not just protecting that legacy; we’re investing in its future by expanding our film and television tax credit, launching a new post-production credit and standing up for performers in the age of AI. "We’re making sure independent filmmakers and the next generation of storytellers and creators have a real shot to build, hire and produce right here in California," he added. "More productions, more good jobs, more California stories told by California workers." CALIFORNIA LAW PUTS DIGITAL FINGERPRINTS ON AI FAKES At the federal level, a bipartisan coalition of lawmakers is working on a tax credit for film and television productions. The bill is expected to be introduced in Congress in early November, with its backers aiming to secure passage by Dec. 11, before the current Congress concludes its work. If passed, the credit would take effect in 2027 and could be used alongside state production incentives. Championed by President Donald Trump, the legislation has also received support from one of his most formidable political opponents, Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif. Schiff led the first impeachment effort against Trump and has remained a vocal critic of his leadership. "I am in strong agreement with the President," Schiff said on X. "Congress should immediately take up and pass a federal film tax incentive to bring back these good-paying jobs that we've lost to other countries." NETFLIX CHIEF ADMITS TRUMP IS HELPING SHOWBIZ INDUSTRY AS FEDERAL TAX CREDIT BILL AIMS TO FUEL HOLLYWOOD JOBS Filmmaker Paul Kampf, a 30-year veteran of the entertainment industry, described California’s incentives as "a really good start." "No matter where you make your film, whether it's Georgia, Delaware, Puerto Rico or Europe, if you can do your post-production in California, you're keeping jobs here, especially in independent films," Kampf told Fox News Digital. "We should be incentivizing filmmakers in America to stay in America. And we should also incentivize filmmakers who are outside of America to do their post here." Kampf, who has produced four feature films and a documentary in Serbia before embarking on his sixth project there, titled "Harvest," has also found himself embroiled in a situation in which a company owned by the Serbian government released the film in Eastern Europe without his permission. "This film is an example of what happens if we don't protect Americans and entice Americans to film here," Kampf said. In California, 35 films, including 28 independent projects, have received production incentives for filming in the state. The sequel to Lionsgate’s blockbuster 2026 hit "Michael" is among the projects, along with a new Pixar film. FILM PRODUCER SAYS 'MADE IN AMERICA' MOVIES CAN HELP REVIVE HOLLYWOOD'S STRUGGLING INDUSTRY All told, the projects are expected to generate more than $1 billion in direct production spending, according to the California Film Commission. "Through our tax credit program, we’re helping bring these stories to the screen while keeping the jobs, investment and production that bring them to life right here in California," Colleen Bell, director of the California Film Commission, said Wednesday in a statement. Kampf, who has made films in several countries, told Fox News Digital California had long been arrogant about its position in the industry, assuming it held a monopoly on filmmaking. "I've made movies all over the world. I don't make movies in LA. I live here. I lived the taxes of LA and California, and I live the sort of challenges of lifestyle here," he said. "I think Hollywood needs a facelift, and it's no pun intended. It needs to be seen as a place that is invigorating and investing in filmmaking again. articles.title: Country star Ella Langley cancels Tulsa, Oklahoma, show due to ‘serious security threat’
articles.summary: Country singer Ella Langley canceled her sold-out show slated for Friday evening in Tulsa, Oklahoma, due to what she described as “a serious security threat.”
articles.body: Country singer Ella Langley canceled her sold-out show slated for Friday evening in Tulsa, Oklahoma, due to what she described as “a serious security threat.” The 27-year-old star announced the last-minute cancellation on Instagram, saying the threat involved “the safety of my fans, the venue staff, and my team.” “The incredibly difficult decision was made to cancel tonight’s show,” she said. “This decision was made under the advisement of local authorities, the venue, and my security team.” Tulsa police said Friday “a call was made threatening the lives of people attending the event.” Police swept the area with its K-9, bomb team, patrol and venue security but did not find anything dangerous, and the building and surrounding area was swept a second time but police “again found no credible threat to the event’s safety,” the department said. Police said that it advised Langley’s staff that no credible threat was found, “but they decided to cancel the performance anyway.” “We apologize to everyone who came down tonight. We appreciate your patience, and it is unfortunate that some nefarious characters successfully disrupted the event, ruining the evening for thousands of people,” police said. The incident remains under investigation. Langley — whose single “Choosin’ Texas” has made history for topping the Billboard Hot 100 for over 23 weeks — apologized to her fans, but stressed safety is paramount. “I know how much time, travel, money, and planning goes into coming to a show, and I can’t tell you how sorry I am. This is not a decision that was made lightly,” she said. “I was so looking forward to spending tonight with you, but your safety will always mean more to me than anything else. I refuse to put anyone in harm’s way,” she continued. The show was set to take place at Tulsa’s BOK Center, which shared the same statement Langley included in her post on social media. “The safety and well-being of everyone involved is our absolutely priority, and after careful consideration, we have determined that the show cannot proceed,” the statement said. “The safety of fans is our foremost concern and will always come first.” The statement said details regarding refunds will be shared soon.

articles.title: Dia das Crianças: veja onde comemorar a data com a garotada no DF | G1
articles.standfirst: Batalha de tintas, peças teatrais, e feira geek são algumas opções de atividades. Veja o que fazer com crianças neste fim de semana e feriado.
articles.summary: Batalha de tintas, peças teatrais, e feira geek são algumas opções de atividades. Veja o que fazer com crianças neste fim de semana e feriado.
articles.body:
Crianças, em imagem de arquivo — Foto: gpointstudio/Magnific

O Dia das Crianças é comemorado nesta segunda-feira (12). No Distrito Federal, muitos estabelecimentos prepararam programações especiais para celebrar a data, começando já neste fim de semana.

O g1 preparou uma lista de sugestões para aproveitar o feriado com a garotada:

Taguatinga Shopping recebe edição de 10 anos do VideoGameShow

SESI Lab celebra Dia das Crianças com circo, teatro e experiências de criatividade

Dia das Crianças tem participação de mascotes e brindes no Nicolândia

Querido Festival reúne música, circo e brincadeiras no fim de semana do Dia das Crianças

Projeto CrianCei reúne crianças e famílias em dia de cultura, lazer e cuidado em Ceilândia

Mané Mercado tem programação especial para as crianças durante todo o mês de outubro

Terraço Shopping celebra Dia das Crianças com três dias de diversão

JK Shopping prepara programação especial para toda a família no mês das crianças

Dia das Crianças ganha histórias, cores e imaginação no Brasília Shopping

Encontro Poké BSB celebra o Dia das Crianças no Centro Cultural TCU

Dia das Crianças com tarde de oficinas e espetáculo no Pontão

Taguatinga Shopping recebe edição de 10 anos do VideoGameShow — Foto: Divulgação

O universo dos games e da cultura geek toma conta do Taguatinga Shopping no fim de semana do Dia das Crianças. Comemorando 10 anos, o VideoGameShow reúne grandes nomes da internet e da dublagem, concursos de cosplay e K-pop, experiências com jogos, feira geek, exposições e atividades interativas.

A edição comemorativa também conta com uma exposição dedicada à história dos videogames. O Museu VideoGameShow reúne mais de 700 consoles de diferentes gerações, incluindo aparelhos desde o primeiro console lançado em 1972 até edições raras de colecionador.

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 90, pelo site

Museu do SESI LAB inova sendo 100% interativo. — Foto: Jomar Bragança

Neste sábado (10) e domingo (11), o SESI Lab comemora o Dia das Crianças com oficinas e teatro de bonecos.

A oficina Parque CircoMania, da trupe Delírio Circense, acontece das 11h às 13h e tem aulas de acrobacias aéreas, ativações para bebês, pernas de pau, malabarismo, desafios mágicos e mais. Já a oficina Pequenos Makers é feita para soltar a criatividade dos pequenos, a partir das 15h.

A partir de 16h, o Giramundo apresenta o espetáculo Pedro e o Lobo na Praça da Árvore. A peça, baseada na obra do compositor russo Sergei Prokofiev, apresenta, com marionetes a fio, a estrutura de uma orquestra e as famílias de instrumentos.

📍 Local: SESI Lab – Setor Cultural Sul, ao lado da Rodoviária do Plano Piloto

A roda gigante da Nova Nicolândia foi inaugurada em 2014 com as cores da bandeira do Brasil para atrair os turistas durante a Copa do Mundo — Foto: Letícia Carvalho/G1

Na segunda-feira (12), das 10h15 às 20h, o Nicolândia tem distribuição de brindes, como balões, broches e tatuagens, além de encontros com o mascote do parque.

Entre as ativações preparadas especialmente para a data estão uma cabine de fotos e um painel interativo, onde as crianças poderão desenhar e deixar a criatividade tomar conta do espaço.

📍 Local: Nicolândia - Parque da Cidade - Brasília (DF)

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$125,96, pelo site

Querido Festival reúne música, circo e brincadeiras no fim de semana do Dia das Crianças — Foto: Divulgação

Neste domingo (11) e segunda-feira (12), música, circo, literatura, contação de histórias e brincadeiras ocupam o Clube do Choro de Brasília, na primeira edição brasiliense do Querido Festival.

Domingo (11), Chou Chou, Grupo Matrakaberta, Irmãos Saúde e Meriele e Sua Gente integram a programação, com o Palhaço Pepino como mestre de cerimônias. As apresentações passam pela música, literatura, contação de histórias e ritmos brasileiros.

No feriado, a programação continua com Chou Chou e Farofa, Will e Alessandra, As Pareias e SQQ Rockids, além do Palhaço Pepino. O segundo dia amplia a mistura de linguagens do festival, com cantigas de roda, circo, cultura popular e rock infantil.

🗓️ Quando: domingo (11) e segunda-feira (12)

⏰ Horário: das 9h às 12h e das 14h às 17h

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 25, pelo site

O Vale Jurássico chegou no Parque da Cidade, dando início à temporada em Brasília. Com dinossauros animatrônicos, ambientes temáticos e atividades interativas, a experiência propõe uma expedição para crianças e adultos.

A experiência começa na recepção e segue por um catamarã cenográfico, que simula o embarque para uma expedição. Na sequência, os visitantes chegam ao Laboratório Jurássico, onde acontece a etapa guiada, antes de seguirem para a Floresta Jurássica, que poderá ser explorada livremente pelas famílias.

Ao longo do percurso, o público encontra dinossauros, exposição e atividades interativas, espaço kids, cenários para fotos e uma área gastronômica temática. O espaço contará ainda com loja oficial de souvenirs e uma área VIP destinada à realização de aniversários.

📍 Local: Estacionamento 5 do Parque da Cidade

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 75, pelo site

Em comemoração ao dia das crianças, neste sábado (10), acontece a 2ª edição do CrianCei – Sementes do Amanhã, no Ponto de Cultura Menino da Ceilândia. A programação gratuita reúne DJ, yoga, oficina de tintas de terra, pintura de rosto, brinquedos infláveis, brincadeiras, entrega de kits e brinquedos e sorteios.

📍 Local: Ponto de Cultura Menino de Ceilândia – Ceilândia/DF

As unidades de Brasília e Águas Claras prepararam uma agenda completa para toda a família, com atividades que vão de oficinas criativas e gastronômicas a apresentações musicais, teatro, recreação e experiências temáticas.

A programação reúne o Clubinho do Mané, com atividades gratuitas, e opções pagas, incluindo ações especiais nas brinquedotecas Manezinho e Brincandoteca. Ao longo do mês, os dois endereços também recebem atrações especiais para celebrar o Dia das Crianças e entram no clima do Halloween, com brincadeiras, oficinas, caracterização, cortejos, caça aos doces, desfiles e espetáculos.

🗓️ Quando: fins de semana e feriado do mês de outubro

📍 Local: Mané Mercado Brasília e Águas Claras

🎫 Programação gratuita, sujeita a lotação, não sendo necessário fazer inscrições

Entre sábado (10) e segunda-feira (12), o Terraço Shopping conta com atrações gratuitas que valorizam o brincar, a criatividade e os momentos compartilhados em família. Um dos destaques é a edição especial do Quintal do Terraço, criado para resgatar as brincadeiras tradicionais e mostrar que a diversão também acontece longe das telas.

O Tardes no Terraço, programação de teatro infantil, também ganha uma edição especial para o feriado. As apresentações começam às 16h e trazem três espetáculos: Guerreiras do Pop Coreano, no sábado; Mônica e sua Turma, no domingo (11); e Pokemundo, na segunda-feira, feriado de Dia das Crianças.

🗓️ Quando: sábado (10), domingo (11) e segunda-feira (12)

Ao longo de todo o mês, o shopping reúne atrações que combinam diversão, cultura, entretenimento e lazer para diferentes idades. A agenda inclui Parque Miraculous com Ladybug e Cat Noir, espetáculos teatrais e atrações circenses.

No feriado, das 12h às 20h, o estacionamento L1 (Marquise), será transformado em um espaço dedicado ao universo circense, com atrações do Circo Artitude.

⏰ Horário: de segunda a sábado, das 10h às 22h; domingos, das 12h às 20h

🎫 Ingressos: para Parque Miraculous, R$ 40 (para 40 minutos), demais atividades gratuitas

Dia das Crianças ganha histórias, cores e imaginação no Brasília Shopping — Foto: Divulgação

No domingo, é a vez da arte tomar conta do estacionamento externo, em frente aos hotéis, das 9h às 11h, com a 5ª edição da Batalha de Tintas. A experiência é aberta ao público.

Para fechar a programação, o Teatro Brasília Shopping recebe, na segunda-feira, às 16h, uma aventura inspirada na Turma dos Cachorros, da Patrulha Canina. Com missões de resgate, veículos especiais e muito humor, o espetáculo acompanha os filhotes em desafios para proteger a comunidade de Adventure Bay.

⏰ Horário: domingo, das 9h às 11h, e segunda, às 16h

🎫 Entrada gratuita. Para a peça teatral, retirar ingresso gratuito pelo aplicativo do shopping

O Encontro Poké BSB especial de Dia das Crianças acontece nesta segunda-feira (12), das 11h às 18h, no Centro Cultural TCU. A programação reúne trocas de cartas, torneios Pokémon TCG, jogos de tabuleiro e sorteios de brindes para divertir fãs, colecionadores e famílias.

A atividade faz parte da programação de Dia das Crianças do Centro Cultural TCU, que contará com a inauguração do novo parquinho infantil. O público também poderá aproveitar cortejo circense, pintura de rosto, esculturas de balão, animação e brincadeiras. Pipoca, algodão-doce e picolé serão distribuídos gratuitamente.

📍 Local: Centro Cultural TCU, (Setor de Clubes Sul, trecho 3)

Nesta segunda-feira (12), das 13h às 17h, a programação no Pontão do Lago Sul conta com oficinas e atividades recreativas conduzidas pela equipe da Broadway Show. Realizadas no Anfiteatro, ao lado do Gran Bier, as atividades são divididas em quatro oficinas, com uma hora de duração cada.

Às 13h, a programação começa com umaa oficina de dança, seguida pela oficina de instrumentos musicais, às 14h. Às 15h, será a vez da oficina de brincadeiras e recreação e, encerrando a tarde, às 16h, acontece a oficina de circo. Cada atividade terá capacidade para até 30 crianças.

📍 Local: Anfiteatro do Pontão do Lago Sul

Estupenda Trupe tem programação gratuita de teatro em outubro

Estupenda Trupe tem programação gratuita de teatro em outubro — Foto: Divulgação

A Cia. Estupenda Trupe realiza duas programações gratuitas de teatro em Brasília durante o mês de outubro. No feriadão do Dia das Crianças, neste sábado (10), o público poderá assistir ao espetáculo João e o Pé de Feijão, às 10h e às 13h, no Jardim Botânico de Brasília.

A programação do Festival Teatro e Sustentabilidade na Infância continua nos dias 17, 24 e 31 de outubro, com outros espetáculos. Já o projeto Memória Candanga – Teatro, Educação e História tem apresentações de Festa do Sol nos dias 13, 15, 19, 20, 22 e 26 de outubro, no Museu Vivo da Memória Candanga, no Núcleo Bandeirante.

As atividades são gratuitas, com sessões acessíveis em Libras e audiodescrição.

🗓️ Quando: de 10 a 31 de outubro, em datas específicas

⏰ Horários: sessões às 10h e às 13h no Jardim Botânico; às 9h30 e às 14h30 no Museu Vivo da Memória Candanga

📍 Local: Jardim Botânico de Brasília e Museu Vivo da Memória Candanga, no Núcleo Bandeirante

The film recorded the earnings across 14,583 shows, taking its total domestic net collection to Rs 260 cr.The movie’s India gross collection has reached Rs 312 cr. It also earned Rs 6 cr from overseas markets on Friday, bringing its cumulative overseas gross to Rs 95 cr. With these earnings, the worldwide gross collection stands at Rs 407 cr.The Day 8 collection marks an 11.5% increase over Thursday’s Rs 13 cr. It earned Rs 53.50 cr on Saturday and Rs 61 cr on Sunday, taking its opening weekend total to Rs 176.50 cr.The collections dropped to Rs 21 cr on Monday and Rs 19.50 cr on Tuesday. The film subsequently earned Rs 15.50 cr on Wednesday and Rs 13 cr on Thursday. These figures brought its first-week India net collection to Rs 245.50 cr.Friday’s earnings pushed the overall India net total to Rs 260 cr. The latest figures indicate a recovery after the weekday decline.'Drishyam 3' day 8 occupancy and footfallsThe Hindi 2D version of 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' recorded an overall theatre occupancy of 17.87% on Friday. Morning shows registered 6.77%, while afternoon occupancy stood at 12.38%. The evening shows recorded 18.15%, followed by the highest occupancy of the day at 31.54% during night shows.The film recorded 582,672 footfalls on Day 8. Its cumulative footfalls across India reached 10,700,076 by the end of Friday. This places its total theatrical admissions above 10.7 million during its first eight days.'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion' story and reviewThe third instalment follows Vijay Salgaonkar, played by Ajay Devgn, as he attempts to protect his family from another determined police investigation. Jaideep Ahlawat joins the story as Rajveer Tomar, a new police officer determined to bring Vijay down.Rajveer believes he possesses fresh evidence that could finally break through Vijay’s carefully constructed defence. His approach is summed up by the line, “System ka darr bana rehna chahiye.” Vijay, meanwhile, understands the challenge of staying ahead of investigators who want to expose his past actions.His response, “Agar hero jail mein gaya, toh audience ko accha lagega?” captures the franchise’s central conflict. The story once again asks viewers to support a protagonist whose actions raise difficult moral questions.Although the film revisits familiar territory, the arrival of a new adversary adds another dimension to Vijay’s continuing battle.The film has also attracted attention for reportedly surpassing the Malayalam original, with early reviews drawing comparisons between the two versions. The screenplay is credited to Aamil Keeyan Khan, Abhishek Pathak and Parveez Shaikh. articles.body: Nani's 'The Paradise' could receive changes ahead of its OTT release, with reports suggesting that the actor is personally monitoring the film's digital version. Directed by Srikanth Odela, the movie attracted considerable attention before its theatrical debut. However, some viewers felt the final product did not meet their expectations.According to 123 Telugu, the team is considering adding scenes that were left out of the theatrical cut. Srikanth Odela had previously spoken about the possibility of changes. It remains unclear which portions could be added or when the revised version will premiere on OTT.The reported plans come as Nani has opened up about the criticism surrounding the film. In an interview with The Hollywood Reporter India, the actor explained why he could understand some of the complaints even before the movie reached theatres.Nani reportedly oversees 'The Paradise' OTT versionNani is reportedly taking a personal interest in preparing 'The Paradise' for its digital release. The proposed changes could include previously unseen shots that were not part of the theatrical version.The movie received mixed reactions, with some viewers expressing disappointment over its content despite the anticipation surrounding the project. Whether the additional footage will address those concerns remains to be seen.Nani says friends and family give honest feedbackSpeaking to The Hollywood Reporter India, Nani explained that the people closest to him do not hesitate to express their opinions about his films. He believes their honesty helps him understand how audiences might respond to his work.“I'm not from a cinema background. The people I'm surrounded with are extremely honest to me. There's no filter at all,” he said. The actor recalled that even some of his successful films did not impress everyone around him. He said these reactions helped him remain connected to the audience rather than viewing moviegoers as a separate group.“My friends and family would say, 'We don't want to watch that film, we didn't like it at all...' So I was always very close to reality… I've always watched films in the theatre; I know that I am one among the audience. I don't think the audience is a separate entity. I always feel that if I like it, they would like it too... I'm one of them,” he said.Actor noticed potential issues before theatrical releaseNani also revealed that he had recognised certain portions of 'The Paradise' that might not work for every viewer. He believed the interval sequence, background score and childhood portions would connect with audiences.However, he was also aware of moments that could affect the film's reception. According to Nani, some of the concerns raised by viewers after the release were issues he had already noticed.“Anything they (the audience) have been mentioning, logically or something where it dipped or something which didn't work for them... I did see all of that. I felt that before,” Nani said.Nani explains how he judges his own workThe actor said he tries to evaluate his films from an audience member's perspective. Maintaining distance from his own work, he explained, helps him recognise which scenes are likely to connect with viewers.“I also knew which portions would work and land… As long as you can be detached from your own work and see it as the audience, it will always be clear. And I don't know how not to do that, I don't know how to get carried away,” he added.'The Paradise' earns Rs 119.54 cr in IndiaMeanwhile, 'The Paradise', featuring Nani and Kayadu Lohar, continued its theatrical run on Friday, October 9. According to Sacnilk, the movie collected Rs 51 lakh in India net earnings on Day 16.Its gross collection for the day stood at Rs 57 lakh across 518 shows, with an overall occupancy rate of 18.2%. The film's cumulative India net collection reached Rs 119.54 cr. The worldwide gross collection stood at Rs 171.96 cr. This includes Rs 140.81 cr from India and Rs 31.15 cr from overseas markets. articles.title: Ryan Reynolds and Colleen Hoover’s alleged texts reveal the actor calling ‘It Ends With Us’ Justin Baldoni a 'predator'
articles.summary: The legal drama between Justin Baldoni and Blake Lively may have ended in a settlement, but the chats and scandalous texts are still leaking online.
articles.body: The legal drama between Justin Baldoni and Blake Lively may have ended in a settlement, but the chats and scandalous texts are still leaking online.This time around, the messages, allegedly sent between Ryan Reynolds and Coleen Hoover, revealed more information about what the two were talking about, specifically regarding Baldoni, as the legal battle blew up on social media.Ryan Reynolds and Colleen Hoover’s texts about Justin Baldoni released onlinePage Six reported that some new texts between Blake Lively’s husband and the author of ‘It Ends With Us’ have come to light through some new court documents. The report stated that this exchange between the two happened on August 10, 2024.In the texts, the ‘Green Lantern’ star allegedly talks about Baldoni’s actions during the legal case, stating, “Yeah, when he uses a crisis team like that, you can start to see all the strategy they’ve equipped him with. Crisis team: okay, Justin, all you do is talk about DV and how wonderful Blake is." And we’ll handle the online stuff. No matter what, you keep up your feminist advocacy. And speak like an emotionally elevated thought leader. Understood?”He also allegedly joked about the actor and director, adding, “Justin: Namaste. Let’s get this b****," and “And I think the truth about him is already finding its way to the light.” The outlet revealed that Hoover had replied to the actor’s messages with a laughing reaction.Ryan Reynolds also called Justin Baldoni a sociopath and a predatorDuring their text exchange, Reynolds also allegedly named Baldoni while talking to Hoover. He shared, “It’s amazing to me that you can have everybody involved with a production completely run away from a person who is obviously a predator and sociopath, and the narrative must first land on why a woman is the problem."Another text exchange was also revealed in the report, with Reynolds and talent agent Warren Zavala also talking about the alleged smear campaign against Lively. In the text messages, Warren talked about how there is a plan to make her (Lively) look bad, saying, “I have to assume they have a cadre of things they plan to utilize within the bounds of production to make her look bad.”To this, the ‘Deadpool’ actor allegedly replied by saying, “They need to frame it the right way! This isn’t hard. The sentence needs to start with… feels like they’re trying to thread the needle. They just need to go ****ing straight at this.”A month ago, the actress was awarded USD 400,000 out of the USD 8 million that she had asked for in damages to be paid by Baldoni. Earlier this year, as the trial between Lively and Baldoni reached courts, the two had suddenly settled on an out-of-court deal, moments before Blake's Met Gala 2026 appearance.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Delhi High Court seeks Salman Khan's response to 'Kala Hiran' producer's plea challenging territorial jurisdiction over Salman Khan's suit seeking to block film's release
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court has issued notice to Salman Khan on a plea filed by producer Amit Jani seeking the return of the actor's suit against the proposed
articles.body: The Delhi High Court has issued notice to Salman Khan on a plea filed by producer Amit Jani seeking the return of the actor's suit against the proposed film 'Kala Hiran – The Battle For Legacy', arguing that the court lacks territorial jurisdiction. According to a recent development, Justice Tejas Karia sought Khan's response to the application, which challenges the court's authority to hear the dispute over the film, reportedly inspired by the actor's 1998 blackbuck poaching case.Delhi High Court issues notice to Salman Khan in 'Kala Hiran' caseAccording to Live Law, Justice Tejas Karia sought Khan's response to the application filed under Order VII Rule 10 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC).The proposed film is reportedly inspired by the 1998 blackbuck poaching case involving Khan. The actor has approached the court seeking to restrain its release, alleging that the film and its promotional material infringe upon his personality and publicity rights.The latest application does not amount to a ruling on whether the Delhi High Court has jurisdiction. The court has sought Khan's response before considering the producer's arguments.Why has the producer challenged the Delhi High Court's jurisdiction?In his application, Jani has argued that neither Khan nor the defendants reside or conduct business within Delhi's territorial jurisdiction. According to the producer, Khan resides in Mumbai, while the defendants are stated to reside or carry on business in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh.Jani has also contended that the mere availability of the film's teasers, posters and other promotional material across India, including Delhi, is insufficient to establish territorial jurisdiction.The application further argues that Khan's suit does not establish that the film's promotional campaign specifically targeted audiences in Delhi or that the actor suffered any distinct injury within the national capital.Jani has also opposed the request to restrain the film's release, arguing that an injunction against a completed cinematographic work is an extraordinary remedy. He has maintained that a short teaser cannot provide a complete assessment of a film's context or overall impact.These are the producer's submissions before the court and have not been established as judicial findings.Producer has also sought a stay on Salman Khan's suitThe jurisdiction plea follows another application filed by Jani, on which the Delhi High Court issued notice earlier in the same week. That application seeks a stay on Khan's suit on the grounds that substantially the same dispute is already pending before the court in an earlier proceeding.As reported by the afore mentioned publication, the producer has argued that the proceedings involve parallel litigation concerning the same proposed film, its promotional material and the alleged infringement of Khan's personality or publicity rights.The latest development is part of the ongoing legal dispute between Khan and the makers of 'Kala Hiran'. The actor's suit seeks to prevent the film's release, while the producer has challenged the maintainability and territorial jurisdiction of the proceedings.'Kala Hiran' was earlier directed to remove its teaser and promotional materialThe dispute has been before the Delhi High Court for several months. In July 2026, the court directed the removal of links to the film's teaser and related promotional material following Khan's objections. The actor had alleged that the film's promotional content contained identifiable references to him and could create a misleading impression about events associated with the blackbuck case.The makers, however, have disputed the basis of Khan's objections. In an earlier hearing in September, the producer's side told the court that the film was not in a releasable state because it had not yet received certification from the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC). The court recorded that submission.The current proceedings concern the producer's applications challenging the continuation of Khan's suit and the court's territorial jurisdiction. The court has not, through the latest notice, finally decided either issue.'Kala Hiran – The Battle For Legacy''Kala Hiran – The Battle For Legacy' is a proposed film written by Amit Jani and directed by Bharat S Shrinate. It is stated to draw inspiration from the 1998 blackbuck poaching case involving Salman Khan, although the makers' portrayal and the actor's objections remain part of the ongoing dispute.The film's listed cast includes Nikunj Aggarwal, Rishabh Arora, Rajesh Dahiya, Ram Gangwar, Naresh Gosain and Prakash Joshi.The project has attracted legal scrutiny over its subject matter and promotional material. Its release remains subject to the ongoing dispute and the certification process, with the producer previously telling the court that the film was not ready for release.Salman Khan's current work slateAway from the 'Kala Hiran' dispute, Salman Khan's upcoming film slate includes 'Maatrubhumi: May War Rest In Peace*, directed by Apoorva Lakhia. The film, initially announced as 'Battle of Galwan', is inspired by the 2020 Galwan Valley clash between Indian and Chinese troops and also stars Chitrangda Singh. As of October 2026, the film remains in post-production, with its final cut and CBFC certification still pending.Khan is also reportedly attached to an action drama tentatively referred to as 'SVC63', directed by Vamshi Paidipally and produced by Dil Raju. Reports have linked Nayanthara, Anil Kapoor and Arvind Swamy to the project, although details should be treated as subject to official confirmation. Khan is also hosting 'Bigg Boss 20.Disclaimer: The information in this report is based on a legal hearing as reported by a third-party source. The details provided represent allegations made by the parties involved and are not proven facts. The case is ongoing, and a final verdict has not been reached. articles.title: 'Whatever negativity you have against him, please get rid of it': 'Ranabaali' producer Ravi Shankar makes an emotional plea to trolls targeting Vijay Deverakonda, urges them to give him a fair chance
articles.summary: Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna are gearing up for the release of their upcoming period action drama, 'Ranabaali', directed by Rahul Sankrityan.
articles.body: Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna are gearing up for the release of their upcoming period action drama, 'Ranabaali', directed by Rahul Sankrityan. Ahead of the film’s theatrical release on October 16, 2026, the makers unveiled its trailer, with producer Ravi Shankar making an emotional appeal to social media users to stop targeting Vijay. He defended the actor’s character and urged people to give the film a fair chance instead of spreading negativity about its lead star.'Ranabaali' producer Ravi Shankar makes an appeal to trollsSpeaking at the trailer launch, Ravi Shankar said he had known Vijay for nearly a decade and described him as a kind person who remains focused on his work. The producer expressed disappointment over the negativity directed at the actor on social media, regardless of what he does.“I have a small request. I have known Vijay for close to a decade now. He has an extraordinary character and is an extraordinary person. I like him a lot; he’s a very nice person and quite soft. But I see people spreading negative propaganda on social media, no matter what he does,” he said.Ravi also questioned why some social media users were criticising the film’s subject before the trailer had even been released. He cited a post questioning whether audiences would be interested in a story about the struggles under British colonial rule.“I recently saw a handle questioning who would watch a story about the struggles during British colonial rule. We haven’t even released the trailer, but you’ve already started,” he said.Producer says Vijay Deverakonda deserves a fair chanceThe producer went on to defend Vijay, saying the actor does not appear to dwell on online criticism and remains committed to his work. He urged those targeting him to reconsider their approach and separate their opinions about the actor from the film itself.“He is a really good person; I’ve never seen him talk ill about anyone or care about any of this. He doesn’t have a world beyond his role and cinema. Whatever negativity you have against him in your heart, please get rid of it,” Ravi added.About 'Ranabaali'Directed by Rahul Sankrityan, 'Ranabaali' features Vijay Deverakonda in the titular role of a Telugu man from Rayalaseema who rises against British rule. The film presents him as a fierce warrior whose struggle unfolds against the backdrop of colonial oppression. Rashmika Mandanna plays Jayamma, Ranabaali’s wife and partner in his struggle. Hollywood actor Arnold Vosloo, best known for playing Imhotep in the 1999 film 'The Mummy', essays the antagonist, Sir Theodore Hector, an English oppressor.The film’s music is composed by Ajay–Atul. 'Ranabaali' is scheduled to release in theatres on October 16, 2026, in Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: ‘The second season will give Gulrukh more agency’: Kritika Kamra on her character’s more empowered and evolving journey in Vijay Varma’s 'Matka King 2'
articles.summary: Kritika Kamra is looking forward to returning as Gulrukh in the second season of 'Matka King'.
articles.body: Kritika Kamra is looking forward to returning as Gulrukh in the second season of 'Matka King'. The actor, who plays a wealthy South Bombay woman drawn into the gambling underworld through her association with Brij Bhatti, played by Vijay Varma, has hinted at a more assertive trajectory for her character in the upcoming season. In an interview with Mid-Day, Kritika spoke about her fascination with complex female characters and how Gulrukh’s growing ambition and self-awareness will give her a stronger voice in 'Matka King 2'.Kritika Kamra on why she is drawn to complex female charactersKritika Kamra said she has always gravitated towards women who are layered, contradictory and difficult to categorise. She found those qualities in Gulrukh, whose vulnerability and ambition coexist with intelligence and strength.“I’ve always been drawn to women who have contradictions and don’t fit neatly into a box. That’s something I recognise in Gulrukh as well. She has vulnerability, ambition, intelligence, and strength. That complexity makes her so compelling to me,” the actor told Mid-Day.'Matka King 2': Kritika Kamra says Gulrukh will have more agencyIn Nagraj Manjule’s series, Gulrukh begins as a well-off woman from South Bombay whose encounter with Brij Bhatti draws her into the high-stakes world of matka gambling. As she becomes increasingly involved in the power dynamics surrounding Brij, her journey also becomes one of self-discovery.Kritika suggested that the next season will give Gulrukh greater control over her decisions, allowing her to move beyond reacting to the people and circumstances around her.“The second season will give Gulrukh more agency and a greater understanding of what she wants. She isn’t just reacting to the world anymore; she is beginning to shape it in her own way,” she said.The development could mark a significant shift for Gulrukh as she navigates a world driven by ambition, influence and power. While the makers have not revealed the full plot of the upcoming season, Kritika’s comments indicate that her character’s growing independence will be an important part of the story.Vijay Varma returns as Brij Bhatti in 'Matka King 2'Vijay Varma will reprise his role as Brij Bhatti in the second season. The first season followed Brij’s rise through Bombay’s matka gambling network in the 1950s, tracing his growing influence in a world shaped by risk, money and power. Vijay’s portrayal of Brij anchored the series, with the actor adopting a period-appropriate look and changing his physique for the role. His return will keep the character at the centre of the continuing story, even as Gulrukh’s journey takes a more assertive turn. Plot details for 'Matka King 2' remain under wraps. However, the title of the first episode, 'Ek Aur Baazi', hints at another round of high-stakes moves in the world of gambling.What to expect from 'Matka King 2'With Kritika Kamra teasing a more empowered Gulrukh and Vijay Varma returning as Brij Bhatti, the second season is poised to continue exploring the personal ambitions and power struggles that shaped the first instalment. While the makers are yet to reveal a release date or further story details, Gulrukh’s evolving agency could become a key part of the next chapter.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Britney Spears releases 'She’ll Never Be Me', an unreleased song she co-wrote with Justin Timberlake before their 2002 breakup ahead of 'Britney' anniversary
articles.summary: Britney Spears surprises fans with the release of 'She’ll Never Be Me', an unreleased song she co-wrote with Justin Timberlake in 2001, just ahead of the 25th anniversary of her iconic album 'Britney'.
articles.body: Britney Spears has surprised fans by releasing 'She’ll Never Be Me', an unreleased song recorded in 2001 and co-written with her then-boyfriend Justin Timberlake. The track arrives ahead of the 25th-anniversary edition of her third studio album, 'Britney', scheduled to be released on November 6, 2026. The release also revisits a chapter in the pop star’s career that remains closely associated with her highly publicised relationship and breakup with Timberlake.Britney Spears drops unreleased song from 2001On Friday, the ‘Toxic’ singer released her new song, ‘She’ll Never Be Me,' worldwide, which had originally been made in 2001. The old song had originally been written for her third studio album titled 'Britney.' Not only that, but it was also co-written with her ex-boyfriend Justin Timberlake. The NSYNC member had also participated in the album on another song, ‘What It’s Like to Be Me,' which he co-wrote and provided the backing vocals for as well.The song's release is part of an overall campaign for the release of her 25th anniversary edition of ‘Britney’ to celebrate its anniversary on November 6. The teaser that was shared on the pop singer’s page read, “We cannot hold it; we cannot control it anymore.: The 'Britney (25th Anniversary Edition)' drops November 6, the 25th anniversary of the album's release in the United States. Follow along...more surprises are coming every week until then!”While talking to MTV at the time, Spears had expressed her nervousness about working with Timberlake. She had stated at the time, "I have to say I was a little nervous at first. But then I just totally forgot that he was my boyfriend, and I just said, ‘Britney, just do the vocals, don’t be nervous’ ... But it ended up being fine, actually.”About Justin Timberlake and Britney SpearsBritney Spears and Justin Timberlake first met on the sets of ‘The Mickey Mouse Club’ back in 1992. The two were together from 1999 to 2002. Timberlake had broken up with the singer over a text message while she had been working on set. At the time, reports had revealed that Spears had been unfaithful to the ‘Mirrors’ singer. His music video for ‘Cry Me A River’ also solidified the rumors at the time.However, in her memoir, ‘The Woman in Me,' which was released in 2023, the singer shared that Timberlake had also been unfaithful to her during their relationship and that she got involved with choreographer Wade Robson after learning of his affairs. In an interview with Diane Sawyer in 2003, Spears had been asked about what happened between her and Timberlake, to which she had answered by saying, “I think everyone has a side of their story, and to make them feel a certain way, to make them feel. I’m not technically saying he’s wrong, but I’m not technically saying he’s right, either." In her memoir, she wrote about how she felt ‘exploited’ because of the incident and the interview.Spears also revealed in the book that she had been pregnant with Timberlake; however, he was not ready for a baby. “But Justin definitely wasn’t happy about the pregnancy. He said we weren’t ready to have a baby in our lives, that we were way too young. If it had been left up to me alone, I never would have done it. And yet Justin was so sure that he didn’t want to be a father.”Similarly, Timberlake had also talked about the music video and Spears in ‘Hindsight: & All the Things I Can’t See in Front of Me,' his memoir, which was released in 2018. He had written, “I’ve been pissed off. I wrote ‘Cry Me a River’ in two hours. I didn’t plan on writing it. The feelings I had were so strong that I had to write it, and I translated my feelings into a form where people could listen and, hopefully, relate to it.”Britney Spears' 'She’ll Never Be Me' is now available to streamThe release of 'She’ll Never Be Me' offers listeners a previously unheard piece of Spears’ musical history as she prepares to mark a milestone for her 2001 album. articles.title: ‘He keeps raising the bar and then jumps over it himself’: Jr NTR wishes 'Varanasi' director SS Rajamouli with a playful throwback picture from their 'RRR' days on his 53rd birthday
articles.summary: Jr NTR has penned a heartfelt birthday wish for filmmaker SS Rajamouli, praising the director for continually raising the bar with his films.
articles.body: Jr NTR has penned a heartfelt birthday wish for filmmaker SS Rajamouli, praising the director for continually raising the bar with his films. As Rajamouli turns 53, the actor took to social media to celebrate their bond, sharing a playful picture of the two together and recalling their association that has produced some of Telugu cinema’s biggest hits, including 'RRR'. Meanwhile, Rajamouli is gearing up for his next ambitious project, 'Varanasi', starring Mahesh Babu, Priyanka Chopra Jonas and Prithviraj Sukumaran.Jr NTR's heartfelt birthday wish for SS RajamouliJr NTR took to X to wish Rajamouli on his birthday, expressing his admiration for the filmmaker’s ability to surpass expectations with every new project. Addressing the director affectionately as Jakkanna, the actor wrote:“Happy Birthday to the man who keeps raising the bar and then jumps over it himself. Love you Jakkanna @ssrajamouli.”The message reflected the warmth between the actor and director, who have collaborated on four films over the years. Their professional association has spanned more than two decades, beginning with Rajamouli’s directorial debut and culminating in the global success of 'RRR'.Jr NTR shares a playful picture with his 'RRR' directorAlong with his birthday message, Jr NTR shared a photograph capturing a light-hearted moment with Rajamouli. In the picture, the filmmaker is seen carrying the actor on his back, offering fans a glimpse of their camaraderie away from the screen. The photograph appears to be from the promotional campaign for 'RRR', their 2022 period action drama that brought their collaboration to a global audience.Jr NTR and SS Rajamouli's successful collaborationsJr NTR and Rajamouli first collaborated on 'Student No. 1' in 2001, which marked the filmmaker’s directorial debut. The film helped establish their association, and they reunited for 'Simhadri' in 2003. The action drama became a major commercial success and further strengthened Jr NTR’s standing as a mass entertainer.Their third collaboration, 'Yamadonga', arrived in 2007. Blending fantasy, action and comedy with elements of mythology, the film added another successful title to their shared filmography.The duo reunited for 'RRR' in 2022, with Jr NTR playing Komaram Bheem and Ram Charan portraying Alluri Sitarama Raju. The film earned international recognition, while its song 'Naatu Naatu', composed by MM Keeravaani, won the Academy Award for Best Original Song in 2023. With four films behind them, the actor-director partnership remains one of the notable collaborations in Telugu cinema, spanning commercial successes and an internationally acclaimed production.SS Rajamouli's next film 'Varanasi' to release in 2027Rajamouli is now preparing for 'Varanasi', his upcoming adventure film starring Mahesh Babu, Priyanka Chopra Jonas and Prithviraj Sukumaran. The ambitious project is expected to traverse multiple timelines and locations across continents, including Africa and Antarctica. The film has generated considerable anticipation given Rajamouli’s track record with large-scale productions such as 'Baahubali' and 'RRR'.
